events.reason: Clothing-growth self-comparison becomes a disastrous school-photo proof; school eligibility now matches the actual premise.

choices.title: The sleeves were innocent
choices.result: The photo confirms it: you have grown. The top has been doing the same job with less and less material to work with.
choices.journal: I realised how much I had grown after comparing an old photo with my clothes.

choices.label: Roll the sleeves and call it fashion
choices.title: Extremely limited edition
choices.result: You commit to the look. It remains a short top, but you stop tugging at it every few seconds.
choices.journal: I rolled up short sleeves and wore the top as it was.

choices.label: Check everyone else’s growth rate

choices.result: Some people are taller. Some are shorter. None of your checking gives your top another centimetre of fabric.

choices.label: Ask for a crop above the lettering
choices.title: Now a very large head
choices.result: The cropped proof removes the slogan and most of your shoulders. You approve it before anyone suggests keeping the original as a wallet photo.
choices.journal: I cropped an embarrassing slogan out of my school photograph.

choices.label: Sign the proof like a celebrity
choices.title: Little Star goes professional
choices.result: You add a sweeping signature and “no interviews”. The joke gets a laugh. You still choose the smallest print size.
choices.journal: I signed my embarrassing Little Star photograph as though I were famous.

choices.label: Inspect everyone else’s proof for worse outfits
choices.title: A thorough investigation
choices.result: You find a blinking face and one unfortunate collar. You spend so long arguing that the photo is “not that bad” that everyone asks to see it.
choices.journal: I drew more attention to my school photograph while hunting for worse ones.

choices.title: Mostly, we smell cheese
choices.result: {parent} laughs and admits they were having a moan. You fix the phone, then both turn towards the sound of the fridge opening.

choices.label: Fix it without mentioning the draft

choices.journal: I fixed {parent}’s phone without making an issue of a private complaint about me.

choices.label: Send their contacts a mocking reading of it

choices.result: {parent} hears their own message in your worst impression of them. They take the phone back and tell you exactly what they think of sharing private messages. Neither of you is laughing.
choices.journal: I sent {parent}’s private complaint to their contacts to humiliate them.

choices.result: The drawing has done nothing new to deserve the review. It was made by a younger you having a good time.

choices.label: Write a formal rejection on the back

choices.label: Destroy the evidence
choices.title: The dinosaur cannot prove anything
choices.result: You tear the letter up, then notice you kept the drawing. It is an excellent dinosaur. You hide it somewhere nobody can ask questions.

events.reason: Unclear windy message becomes a terrible parental impersonation used to claim chores; remote binding and immediate negotiated work stay factual.

before.body: {parent} sends a voice message. The wind gets most of the speaking time. You can make out your name and something about later.

choices.label: Ask for the details as text
choices.title: The wind leaves the conversation
choices.result: {parent} sends a short message you can read. It answers the question the recording had been trying to ask.
choices.journal: I asked {parent} to resend a windy voice message as text.

choices.label: Arrange a time to talk properly
choices.title: A clearer conversation
choices.result: You speak when you can both hear each other. The original message was mostly a question about your day.
choices.journal: I arranged a proper conversation with {parent} after a windy voice message.

choices.label: Reply as though you understood
choices.title: An unlikely answer
choices.result: {parent} asks what your reply means. You still need to ask what the recording said.
choices.journal: I guessed at a voice message from {parent} instead of asking.

after.title: That is definitely your voice
after.body: {parent} sends a voice note pretending to be you: “I would love to do all the washing-up forever.” Their impression makes you sound like a distressed goose.

choices.label: Request a less insulting goose
choices.title: A second audition
choices.result: {parent} sends a deeper version. Now you sound like a goose with a cold. You both give up trying to discuss the dishes.
choices.journal: I demanded a better impression after {parent} impersonated me in a voice note.

choices.label: Offer one actual round of washing-up
choices.title: Forever has been renegotiated
choices.result: {parent} accepts one evening. You wash up later, with the original recording playing beside the sink. The goose does not offer to dry.
choices.journal: I negotiated one evening of washing-up after {parent} sent a fake promise in my voice.

choices.label: Send an impression of them volunteering instead
choices.title: A household of terrible actors
choices.result: {parent} replies, “I sound nothing like that.” You send their goose back. The exchange ends with two laughing voice notes and no volunteers.
choices.journal: I answered {parent}’s fake voice note with an equally bad impression of them.

events.reason: To-do-list procrastination becomes a chore-dodging dummy caught in a parental lecture; real parent binding added and all outcomes finish immediately.

before.title: The plan needs another colour
before.body: You promised to finish everything by Sunday. Sunday is nearly over. You have completed six versions of the to-do list, including a colour key.

choices.label: Finish one task without making a new list
choices.title: An unexpected practical development
choices.result: One thing actually gets done. You resist the urge to redesign the tick beside it.
choices.journal: I stopped revising a to-do list and completed one task.

choices.label: Cross out half the tasks without remorse
choices.title: The list finally fits
choices.result: Some plans are simply not happening tonight. Admitting it gives you room to stop; it does not complete the crossed-out tasks.
choices.journal: I cut an unrealistic evening plan instead of trying to finish everything.

choices.label: Declare an all-nighter. Design a new schedule.
choices.title: Version seven is beautiful
choices.result: You move between tasks, headings and snacks. Very little gets finished, but the colour key has become exceptional.
choices.journal: I exhausted myself planning too much and finishing very little.

after.title: Your stand-in has a meeting
after.body: To dodge chores, you left a dummy in your dressing gown at your desk. {parent} is now giving it a serious talk about responsibility. The dummy is handling it well.

choices.label: Step out and take over the discussion
choices.title: A noticeable improvement in posture
choices.result: {parent} says the dummy already agreed to take the rubbish out. You do it while the dummy remains at the desk, apparently thinking about its future.
choices.journal: I replaced a dummy during {parent}’s lecture and did the chore it had agreed to.

choices.label: Leave a second dummy to play {parent}
choices.title: A surprisingly peaceful household
choices.result: {parent} watches you arrange both dummies, then hands the real you a rubbish bag. The two stand-ins remain deep in discussion.
choices.journal: I made a second dummy to answer the first one and still had to do my chores.

choices.label: Stay hidden and let the dummy handle it
choices.title: The witness is uncooperative
choices.result: {parent} removes the dressing gown, finds a cushion, and addresses the rest of the lecture to your hiding place. You have to wait for it to finish before coming out.
choices.journal: I hid while {parent} discovered my chore-dodging dummy.

events.reason: Replace repeated interruptions with an unconsented live podcast whose three responses terminate the broadcast differently.

before.title: The rest of your sentence

choices.label: Say you would like to finish the thought

choices.result: {friend} apologises and waits. You finally reach the part you wanted to say.
choices.journal: I asked {friend} to let me finish speaking.

choices.label: Listen, then return to your point
choices.title: A patient detour
choices.result: You acknowledge the connection and bring the conversation back. Both stories get an ending.
choices.journal: I brought a wandering conversation with {friend} back to my point.

choices.label: Interrupt louder
choices.title: Two opening sentences
choices.result: For a moment you are both talking. Neither explanation becomes clearer.
choices.journal: I tried to out-interrupt {friend}.

after.title: People I can fix
after.body: During a video call, {friend} introduces you as the guest on their new podcast. Then you notice the LIVE badge. The episode is called “People I Can Fix”.

choices.label: Announce that the guest did not consent
choices.title: A very short first episode
choices.result: {friend} ends the stream and apologises. You suggest fixing the part where they ask before broadcasting people.
choices.journal: I made {friend} stop broadcasting our call without permission.

choices.label: Introduce the host as your first repair project
choices.title: The host requires parts
choices.result: You diagnose {friend} with an advanced need to hear their own voice. They laugh, end the stream and agree the title needs work.
choices.journal: I turned {friend}’s surprise podcast interview back on its host.

choices.label: Pretend to be an extremely boring sponsor

choices.journal: I sabotaged {friend}’s unannounced live interview with a fake grout advert.

events.reason: Replace a vague disliked nickname with a fraudulent Human Kettle talent-show entry and three distinct cancellations.

before.title: Please do not let that catch on

choices.journal: I told {friend} I preferred my own name.

choices.result: {friend} laughs and agrees. The nickname has an admirably short career.
choices.journal: I gently retired a nickname {friend} had invented.

choices.label: Laugh along despite disliking it

after.title: The human kettle

choices.label: Make them withdraw the entry
choices.title: No boiling tonight
choices.result: {friend} cancels the entry while you watch. Your only public performance is an extremely convincing disappointed stare.
choices.journal: I made {friend} withdraw a talent-show entry they submitted for me.

choices.label: Send {friend} a full kettle audition
choices.title: A rising whistle
choices.result: Your performance starts with a simmer and ends with a scream. {friend} laughs so hard they forget to forward it; you cancel the entry yourself.
choices.journal: I sent {friend} a ridiculous kettle impression before cancelling the contest entry.

choices.label: Draft their entry as “The Human Toilet”

choices.result: You send {friend} your proposed introduction, complete with sound effects. They cancel your entry and ask you never to perform theirs.
choices.journal: I answered {friend}’s kettle prank with a proposed toilet performance.

events.reason: Replace inert silence with a fake wedding website, serious trust damage and the option to end the actual friendship.

before.title: Nothing needs saying

choices.label: Make them delete it and correct the announcement
choices.title: Cancelled before the imaginary cake
choices.result: {friend} deletes the site and posts a correction. You are not engaged by prank, but trusting them with a joke will take longer.
choices.journal: I made {friend} delete a fake wedding website and correct the claim.

choices.label: Request a divorce from the website

choices.journal: I answered {friend}’s fake wedding website with a mock breakup statement.

choices.label: End the friendship. They can keep the website.
choices.title: One real ending
choices.result: You tell {friend} the joke crossed a line and end the friendship. Their imaginary wedding has cost them an actual friend.
choices.journal: I ended my friendship with {friend} over a fake wedding website.

choices.label: Join the movement lying down

choices.journal: I joined {friend}’s anti-chair movement by lying on the floor.

choices.label: Narrate their eventual sit like a sporting defeat

choices.result: When {friend} finally sits, you deliver a full commentary on the collapse of their principles. They get up and choose a seat farther away from you.
choices.journal: I mocked {friend}’s anti-chair principles with sports commentary when they sat down.

choices.journal: I gave confident directions to chairs I had never seen.

after.title: Inside the chicken
after.body: The festival mascot has quit. A volunteer thrusts a chicken suit at you and offers cash for one hour. The head smells of onions. Something inside it is still warm.

choices.label: Tell them you only came for the stalls
choices.title: A civilian again
choices.result: The volunteer apologises and puts the chicken head on a traffic cone. A child immediately asks the cone for a photo.
choices.journal: I declined an emergency shift inside a festival chicken.

choices.label: Wear the chicken suit for {money}
choices.title: Poultry wages
choices.result: You spend an hour being hugged, punched and asked where eggs come from. You collect {money} and peel off the head. Fresh air has never tasted so expensive.
choices.journal: I earned {money} as an emergency chicken mascot.

choices.label: Carry the head around and ask if anyone knows it
choices.title: The missing chicken
choices.result: You announce that you found it wandering alone. The volunteer retrieves the suit before you can organise a search for its body.
choices.journal: I carried a mascot head around a festival as lost property.

events.reason: An accidental wave was too slight to carry three decisions and results.

before.title: A wave with another destination
before.body: Someone across the square waves enthusiastically. You wave back before noticing the person directly behind you carrying an enormous reunion balloon.

choices.label: Laugh and lower your hand
choices.title: A brief public misunderstanding
choices.result: The stranger smiles back. The balloon receives the reunion it was dressed for.
choices.journal: I survived waving at someone who was waving past me.

choices.label: Give the balloon a wave too
choices.title: Everyone is included
choices.result: The balloon’s owner waves back. You have accidentally made the exchange less awkward.
choices.journal: I included a reunion balloon in an accidental greeting.

choices.label: Pretend you were stretching
choices.title: A highly specific stretch
choices.result: You extend the performance longer than any sensible shoulder exercise requires.
choices.journal: I turned an accidental wave into an unconvincing stretch.

after.title: The local cryptid
after.body: {friend} has posted a recording of you snoring under the caption “Unidentified beast heard nearby”. People are debating whether you are a wild boar or faulty plumbing.

choices.label: Record a formal statement from the beast
choices.title: No further grunts
choices.result: You growl that the beast wants privacy and a better pillow. {friend} adds your statement. The plumbing faction refuses to concede.
choices.journal: I answered a friend’s snoring video with a statement from the supposed beast.

choices.label: Post their worst karaoke recording
choices.title: Two endangered species
choices.result: You upload {friend} attempting a high note. They delete your snoring video and demand you delete theirs. You both spend dinner refusing to touch your phones.
choices.journal: I retaliated against a friend’s snoring video with their terrible karaoke.

choices.label: Make them take the recording down
choices.title: Extinct online
choices.result: {friend} removes the clip and apologises. Someone asks where the beast went. You let them worry about the plumbing.
choices.journal: I made a friend remove a recording they posted without asking me.

events.reason: Pigeon surveillance premise has an original escalation and three specific comic payoffs.

before.title: Any difficult questions?
before.body: At a free talk, a speaker claims nobody has ever disproved their theory. The theory is that pigeons remember your face and discuss you at night.

choices.label: Ask how they interviewed the pigeons
choices.title: The method needs work
choices.result: They admit they inferred the conversations. You learn the difference between a suspicious bird and actual evidence.
choices.journal: I questioned the evidence behind a speaker’s theory about pigeons.

choices.label: Let another questioner take this one
choices.title: A useful follow-up
choices.result: Someone asks where the night meetings happen. The speaker says the location is confidential. You take fewer notes after that.
choices.journal: I listened to questions at an implausible public talk.

choices.label: Announce that the pigeons work for you
choices.title: An unexpected disclosure
choices.result: Half the room laughs. The other half wants proof of your authority over pigeons. You have joined the problem.
choices.journal: I interrupted a strange talk by claiming to command pigeons.

events.reason: Queue arbitration offered generic delay management rather than a memorable situation.

before.title: Two queues, one doorway
before.body: Two short queues reach the same narrow doorway. Both groups seem certain they arrived first. Neither has appointed a historian.

choices.label: Suggest taking alternate turns
choices.title: A workable treaty
choices.result: People begin moving again. The debate loses its audience one person at a time.
choices.journal: I suggested alternating two queues at a narrow doorway.

choices.label: Step back and let it settle
choices.title: A little more waiting
choices.result: You lose a few places and keep your calm. Eventually the doorway becomes a doorway again.
choices.journal: I waited out an argument about who reached a queue first.

choices.label: Declare your queue the original
choices.title: A disputed founding document
choices.result: Someone disputes your account immediately. You are now part of the delay you wanted to end.
choices.journal: I joined an argument about a queue’s historical legitimacy.

after.title: The accidental millionaire
after.body: At a charity auction, someone mistakes you for a wealthy donor. The auctioneer hands you the microphone beside a photograph of an elderly donkey. “How much will you give?” The room goes quiet.

choices.label: Admit your wealth has been exaggerated
choices.title: A donkey-sized misunderstanding
choices.result: You explain that you were looking for the toilets. The auctioneer takes back the microphone and points down the corridor. Several people applaud your honesty. One applauds the donkey.
choices.journal: I admitted I was not the wealthy donor a charity auction expected.

choices.label: Donate {money} to the donkey charity
choices.title: A very expensive nod
choices.result: You pay {money}. The auctioneer announces that you have sponsored the donkey’s dental care. You had been hoping it would at least get a holiday.
choices.journal: I donated {money} towards an elderly donkey’s care.

choices.label: Claim you are the donkey’s lawyer
choices.title: Your client declines comment
choices.result: You object to the use of your client’s photograph. The auctioneer asks which law firm you represent. You say “Hee Haw & Partners” and surrender the microphone.
choices.journal: I pretended to represent a donkey at a charity auction.

events.reason: Incorrect map sticker produced three variations on noticing a trivial error.

before.title: You are here, allegedly
before.body: A neighbourhood noticeboard has a map of {city}. Its “You are here” sticker points confidently to a patch of water.

choices.label: Mention it to the caretaker
choices.title: Dry land restored
choices.result: The caretaker checks the orientation and moves the sticker. No rescue boat is required.
choices.journal: I reported a misleading neighbourhood map in {city}.

choices.label: Work out the map’s orientation
choices.title: A small navigation puzzle
choices.result: Once you turn your viewpoint around, the streets line up. The sticker remains unusually aquatic.
choices.journal: I figured out a confusing neighbourhood map.

choices.label: Argue with the sticker
choices.title: The sticker declines to answer
choices.result: A passer-by watches you explain that you are plainly not underwater. The map offers no rebuttal.
choices.journal: I held a brief argument with an incorrect map sticker.

after.title: Your murderous past
after.body: A walking-tour guide points straight at you and tells the group you are the ghost of a notorious murderer. You are outside a shop in {city}, holding a sandwich.

choices.label: Explain that you are alive and eating lunch
choices.title: New evidence
choices.result: The guide calls your sandwich an unsettling detail. You take a large bite. A tourist asks whether ghosts can eat cheese. The guide moves the group along.
choices.journal: I corrected a walking tour that mistook me for a murderer’s ghost in {city}.

choices.label: Ask what crimes you supposedly committed
choices.title: A busy afterlife
choices.result: The guide gives you six victims and a secret tunnel. You ask whether you could have a day off. Someone writes this down as part of the legend.
choices.journal: I listened to a tour guide invent my murderous past.

choices.label: Follow the tour without breaking eye contact
choices.title: The haunting is mobile
choices.result: You trail the group around the corner, chewing slowly. The guide abandons the next stop and ushers everyone into a brightly lit café.
choices.journal: I followed a ghost tour after its guide claimed I was the ghost.

events.reason: Mistaken sign-up was a slight name mix-up; replaced with a public caricature humiliation and three different physical portrait payoffs. Final editorial review removed the repeated fake-laugh recording premise already covered by friend-fake-laugh-rehearsal.

before.title: Your name is on the list
before.body: At a free open-mic afternoon, the host reads out a name very close to yours. People turn towards you. You came to listen.

choices.label: Point out the mistaken name
choices.title: The intended performer appears
choices.result: Someone else stands up, clutching a poem. You applaud with the enthusiasm of a person narrowly spared a stage.
choices.journal: I corrected an open-mic mix-up and stayed in the audience.

choices.label: Offer one very short joke
choices.title: An unexpected guest appearance
choices.result: The host gives you a moment. Your joke gets a laugh, and you hand the microphone back.
choices.journal: I made an unplanned joke at an open mic.

choices.label: Study the floor intensely
choices.title: An unhelpful carpet
choices.result: The host repeats the name. The carpet supplies neither an escape route nor a convincing answer.
choices.journal: I tried to disappear into the floor during an open-mic mix-up.

after.title: A striking resemblance
after.body: A caricaturist at a street fair in {city} offers you a free sample portrait. A small crowd gathers. The artist turns the drawing around. It is you as an enormous angry thumb.

choices.label: Ask whether they could add a jawline
choices.title: The formal thumb
choices.result: The artist adds a bow tie. You point out that this is not a jawline. A spectator says the resemblance is uncanny. You leave holding a thumb in evening wear.
choices.journal: I asked a caricaturist to correct my portrait and received a thumb in a bow tie.

choices.label: Ask for a pencil and draw the artist
choices.title: An exchange of likenesses
choices.result: You draw the artist as a single nostril. They pin both portraits side by side. The crowd laughs. The artist takes back the pencil before you can start on their customers.
choices.journal: I answered an insulting caricature by drawing the artist as a nostril.

choices.label: Cover the portrait and leave
choices.title: One more for the album
choices.result: You fold the drawing and hurry away. The artist’s assistant catches up with a second sketch: the same thumb, running. You fold that one too.
choices.journal: I tried to hide an unflattering caricature and was handed a second one.

events.reason: A watched pen had no meaningful decision or relationship consequence.

before.title: The ceremonial pen
before.body: At a community signing-in desk, someone lends you a pen and then watches as though it has been in their family for several generations.

choices.label: Sign and return it promptly
choices.title: Custody transferred safely
choices.result: They test the pen immediately. It appears to have survived writing your name.
choices.journal: I returned a very carefully supervised borrowed pen.

choices.label: Ask whether it is special
choices.title: A perfectly ordinary favourite
choices.result: It is their only pen that works. The explanation makes the supervision easier to understand.
choices.journal: I asked why a borrowed pen was receiving such close attention.

choices.label: Pocket it without thinking
choices.title: A swift reminder
choices.result: They ask for it back before you reach the door. You return it under considerably closer supervision.
choices.journal: I nearly walked away with someone’s favourite pen.

after.title: Friendship, itemised
after.body: {friend} brings you an invoice for years of friendship. It includes unsolicited advice, waiting outside a toilet and “emotional wear on my sofa”. They slide over a pen and ask you to acknowledge the debt.

choices.label: Hand back the pen and end the friendship
choices.title: Account closed
choices.result: You say that a friendship with a billing department is not one you want. {friend} tears up the invoice. You leave before they can charge for the paper.
choices.journal: I ended my friendship with {friend} after they presented an invoice for it.

choices.label: Ask them to explain every charge
choices.title: The sofa cannot testify
choices.result: You dispute the toilet-waiting rate and ask whether their advice came with a warranty. {friend} starts laughing at “sofa depreciation” and tears up the bill.
choices.journal: I audited a friend’s absurd friendship invoice until we both laughed at it.

choices.label: Write “paid in compliments” across it
choices.title: An unacceptable currency
choices.result: You praise their handwriting and return the invoice. {friend} says you never take them seriously. You say their sofa has excellent credit control. Nobody laughs this time.
choices.journal: I mocked a friend’s invoice instead of asking why they were keeping score.

events.reason: An incorrect forecast repeated the same joke after every option.

before.title: Zero chance of rain
before.body: A stranger at a public weather display tells you rain is impossible today. A drop lands on the forecast. They call it “local moisture”.

choices.label: Suggest looking outside the forecast
choices.title: An awkward update
choices.result: You point to a growing puddle. They concede that the moisture is becoming quite local to everyone.
choices.journal: I questioned a confident weather prediction while it rained.

choices.label: Head for shelter and wave them over
choices.title: Dry and tactful
choices.result: They join you under cover while insisting this does not count as proper rain. You let the roof settle the practical question.
choices.journal: I shared a sheltered spot during an argument about rain.

choices.label: Back them loudly as the rain gets heavier
choices.title: Two experts, no umbrella
choices.result: You both explain the absence of rain while getting visibly wet. The remaining audience moves indoors.
choices.journal: I defended an obviously wrong forecast in the rain.

after.title: The door does not believe in you
after.body: An automatic shop door refuses to open for you. It opens for a child, a trolley and a blowing receipt. You step forward. Nothing. The cashier points at the sensor and suggests waving.

choices.label: Ask the cashier to let you out
choices.title: Assisted departure
choices.result: The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.
choices.journal: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

choices.label: Follow the trolley out
choices.title: Cargo recognised
choices.result: You walk close behind a shopper’s trolley. The door opens. The shopper asks whether you need a lift any farther. You decline at the pavement.
choices.journal: I escaped an automatic door by following a trolley.

choices.label: Perform an increasingly furious dance
choices.title: Movement detected, eventually
choices.result: You squat, clap and flap both arms. The door opens while you are taking a bow. The cashier is already pretending not to have watched.
choices.journal: I danced in front of an automatic door until it acknowledged me.

events.reason: Restarting paper folding was a small procedural task with interchangeable lessons.

before.title: The important page is last
before.body: You are trying a small paper-folding project at a free workshop. The final instruction says to begin with the paper the other way up.

choices.label: Unfold it and begin again
choices.title: Now the instructions agree
choices.result: The second attempt takes less time. You have learned both the shape and the location of the important warning.
choices.journal: I restarted a paper project after finding the crucial instruction last.

choices.label: Turn the mistake into another shape
choices.title: A new species of paper object
choices.result: It is not the example on the table. It does stand up, which feels like a defensible design goal.
choices.journal: I turned a paper-folding mistake into my own design.

choices.label: Explain why the paper is defective
choices.title: A difficult case to prove
choices.result: The person beside you folds the same paper correctly. Your argument loses a useful witness.
choices.journal: I blamed the paper for not reading the instructions.

after.title: Not the tabletop version
after.body: At a craft workshop, you pull the tab on a kit labelled “decorative boat”. A full-size inflatable canoe starts filling the room. The tiny instruction sheet says to inflate outdoors.

choices.label: Deflate it before it reaches the doorway
choices.title: A long public fart
choices.result: You open the valve. The canoe collapses over eight uninterrupted seconds of rude noise. The instructor waits until everyone has stopped laughing to explain the warning.
choices.journal: I deflated a full-size canoe during a crowded craft workshop.

choices.label: Climb in and ask for paddles
choices.title: Dry dock
choices.result: You sit in the canoe while six people finish paper flowers around you. The instructor slides over two wooden spoons and asks you to stop blocking the glue.
choices.journal: I sat in an accidentally inflated canoe while a craft workshop continued around me.

choices.label: Insist the picture on the box was misleading
choices.title: The scale becomes clearer
choices.result: The instructor points to a man in the picture. You had thought he was a decorative speck. Everyone helps flatten your very large ornament.
choices.journal: I argued that a full-size canoe had looked smaller on its box.

choices.title: A manageable correction
choices.result: The host repeats it correctly and moves on. The proposed nickname retires before its first appearance.
choices.journal: I corrected my name instead of accepting an unwanted nickname.

choices.label: Turn the correction into a light joke
choices.title: The right name gets a laugh
choices.result: The host laughs, tries again and gets it right. You keep both your name and the conversation moving.
choices.journal: I made a gentle joke while correcting my name.

choices.label: Use the nickname for the afternoon
choices.title: An unexpectedly long afternoon
choices.result: People keep using it. You begin to understand why small corrections are easier when made early.
choices.journal: I accepted a nickname I did not actually like.

events.reason: Stairs versus a familiar route had no concrete event payoff or meaningful risk.

before.title: The shortcut has several stairs
before.body: A sign promises a shortcut across a public building. Around the next corner, the route becomes a staircase with ambitious ideas about height.

choices.label: Take the familiar accessible route
choices.title: A more predictable journey
choices.result: You return to the route you understand. The sign keeps its optimistic definition of short.
choices.journal: I chose a familiar route over a questionable shortcut.

choices.label: Explore at a comfortable pace
choices.title: The building has another side
choices.result: You learn where the stairs lead and take your time. It is a discovery rather than a race.
choices.journal: I explored a public building’s unexpectedly elaborate shortcut.

choices.label: Hurry to prove the sign right
choices.title: The shortcut wins the argument
choices.result: You arrive tired and mildly offended. The sign has no mechanism for receiving your complaint.
choices.journal: I rushed through a shortcut that did not feel shorter.

after.title: A shortcut through the execution
after.body: A museum shortcut in {city} takes you through a medieval punishment exhibit. A mechanical executioner swings a foam axe across the marked path. The long route has no executioner.

choices.label: Take the long route
choices.title: A head start
choices.result: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.
choices.journal: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

choices.label: Time the swing and walk through slowly
choices.title: A measured execution
choices.result: You wait for the axe to pass, then walk across. The speaker screams anyway. You bow to the watching visitors before reading the next label.
choices.journal: I timed my way past a mechanical executioner at a museum.

choices.label: Sprint straight through the swinging axe
choices.title: Foam has ambitions
choices.result: The axe clips your shoulder. You land against a padded post with a painful thud. An attendant pauses the machine and shows you the sign asking visitors to walk.
choices.journal: I hurt my shoulder racing through a museum’s mechanical executioner.

events.reason: Holding a banner was a generic helper task with little to distinguish it.

before.title: A very small responsibility
before.body: A community volunteer asks you to hold one end of a banner for a minute. The wind immediately applies for the other end.

choices.label: Hold it while they secure it
choices.title: A cooperative wind problem
choices.result: You work out a steadier angle together. The banner eventually becomes readable rather than airborne.
choices.journal: I helped secure a wind-blown community banner.

choices.label: Suggest waiting for the gust to pass
choices.title: A temporary ceasefire
choices.result: A calmer moment arrives. The same task becomes much easier without an argument with the weather.
choices.journal: I suggested waiting for calmer weather before lifting a banner.

choices.label: Let go without warning
choices.title: A sudden solo performance
choices.result: The volunteer catches the loose end. Their expression explains the value of giving notice.
choices.journal: I let go of a banner before warning the person beside me.

after.title: A beautiful baby cabbage
after.body: A fair organiser needs one more judge for a vegetable baby contest. Someone pushes a cabbage in a bonnet towards you. Its grower is waiting for a score and looks ready to take this personally.

choices.label: Judge the cabbage’s personality
choices.title: A quiet, grounded child
choices.result: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.
choices.journal: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

choices.label: Disclose that you eat cabbage
choices.title: A conflict of interest
choices.result: The grower snatches the bonnet shut. The organiser moves you to judging flower arrangements. You are asked whether you eat those too.
choices.journal: I disqualified myself from a vegetable baby contest by admitting I eat cabbage.

choices.label: Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact
choices.title: The parent complains
choices.result: The grower says the cabbage is shy. You suggest public speaking lessons. The organiser takes back your scorecard before the turnip reaches you.
choices.journal: I was removed as a vegetable baby judge after criticising a cabbage’s eye contact.

choices.journal: I corrected a memory that had borrowed a scene from a film.

choices.label: Stick to the part you remember clearly

choices.result: You leave out the uncertain details. The story becomes less spectacular and easier to believe.
choices.journal: I separated a clear memory from uncertain embellishment.

choices.label: Continue towards the dramatic ending
choices.title: A familiar screenplay
choices.result: A listener supplies the next line. You discover that your memory has an unusually recognisable cast.
choices.journal: I continued a doubtful memory until someone recognised the film.

events.reason: Routine seat swapping offered a predictable polite/polite/rude structure.

before.title: The best seat in the room
before.body: You arrive early for a free event and find the seat with the clearest view. Someone asks whether you could move so their group can sit together.

choices.label: Move to another available seat
choices.title: A small rearrangement
choices.result: They thank you and make room. Your new seat has a slightly worse view and a much quieter neighbour.
choices.journal: I moved seats so a group could sit together.

choices.label: Politely keep the seat
choices.title: A reasonable answer
choices.result: You explain that you chose it carefully. They look for another arrangement without a scene.
choices.journal: I politely kept a seat I had arrived early to choose.

choices.label: Explain the principles of arriving early
choices.title: More than a seating answer
choices.result: The group moves elsewhere before you finish your argument about punctuality.
choices.journal: I gave a lecture when a simple answer about a seat would have done.

after.title: The important businessman
after.body: You sit in the last free café chair. A child wearing an enormous tie tells you it is reserved for an important businessman. The businessman, they explain, is them.

choices.label: Ask what business they are in
choices.title: A volatile juice market
choices.result: They explain that juice has gone up and crayons are a bad investment. You move to the counter while they hold a meeting with a biscuit.
choices.journal: I gave up a café chair after hearing a child’s business plan.

choices.label: Offer them the chair after your drink
choices.title: A hard negotiation
choices.result: They demand a deadline. You point to the remaining drink. They watch every sip, checking an upside-down plastic watch.
choices.journal: I negotiated a café chair with a child dressed as a businessman.

choices.label: Explain that reserving chairs is bad business
choices.title: The consultant is dismissed
choices.result: You begin discussing customer relations. The child yawns and asks their adult to find a less talkative chair. You finish your drink in peace, slightly wounded.
choices.journal: I lost a business argument to a child over a café chair.

before.title: A reminder that needs reminding
before.body: You find a note you wrote to help remember something important. It says only, “The usual one, but different.”

choices.label: Write a clearer private reminder
choices.title: Future you gets better information
choices.result: You replace the riddle with a useful explanation and keep it somewhere appropriate.
choices.journal: I replaced an unhelpful private reminder with a clear one.

choices.label: Work backwards from the context
choices.title: An investigation into your own shorthand
choices.result: The surrounding notes help you understand what you meant. You remain an unreliable witness to your own abbreviation.
choices.journal: I reconstructed the meaning of an obscure note to myself.

choices.label: Assume it will make sense later

choices.result: The note remains exactly as informative as before. You have postponed the same puzzle.
choices.journal: I left a confusing reminder for my future self to solve.

events.reason: Lost-property handling read like instructions rather than a playable comic incident.

before.title: One glove, several possibilities
before.body: You spot a single glove on a public bench. A nearby notice asks people to leave found items at the building’s reception desk.

choices.label: Take it to reception
choices.title: A findable lost item
choices.result: The receptionist adds it to the found-items box. Its owner now has somewhere sensible to ask.
choices.journal: I took a lost glove to the nearby reception desk.

choices.label: Leave it visible on the bench
choices.title: Ready for a retraced route
choices.result: You make sure it is easy to see. Someone returning along the same path may still spot it.
choices.journal: I left a lost glove where its owner might retrace their steps.

choices.label: Question everybody about the glove
choices.title: A small unnecessary investigation
choices.result: Several strangers confirm that they have hands. Reception is still the most promising lead.
choices.journal: I made a lost glove into a larger investigation than necessary.

after.title: The lost hand
after.body: You pick up a glove from a bench. A rubber hand slides out of its sleeve. It has painted fingernails, a wristwatch and no obvious owner.

choices.label: Carry it to reception
choices.title: Please wave if this is yours
choices.result: The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.
choices.journal: I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

choices.label: Leave it upright on the bench
choices.title: A welcoming bench
choices.result: You prop the hand up like a greeting. A passer-by gives it a cautious high five. The returning magician looks offended that you found a better use for it.
choices.journal: I propped a lost rubber hand up for high fives.

choices.label: Ask around for anyone missing a hand
choices.title: A very literal description
choices.result: People hide their hands as you approach. The magician catches up with you and asks you to stop advertising his equipment like a crime scene.
choices.journal: I carried a rubber hand around asking who had lost it.

events.reason: Introductions were a generic concision lesson with little character or surprise.

before.title: A biography of thirty seconds
before.body: Before a discussion circle begins, the host asks everyone for a very short introduction. The first person has already described three previous homes.

choices.label: Give your name and one interest
choices.title: Plenty to begin with
choices.result: Someone asks about the interest later. Your introduction leaves room for an actual conversation.
choices.journal: I kept a group introduction short enough to start a conversation.

choices.label: Add a question for the group
choices.title: An invitation instead of a résumé
choices.result: Other people begin answering. You learn more by making room for them.
choices.journal: I used an introduction to ask other people about themselves.

choices.label: Attempt the most impressive biography
choices.title: An introduction with several chapters
choices.result: You run past the time limit while explaining that you are usually very concise.
choices.journal: I overprepared my own introduction and forgot to stop.

after.title: Everyone here is a winner
after.body: At a motivational taster session, you are asked to name your greatest achievement. The person before you says they survived eight workplace investigations. The facilitator applauds and turns to you.

choices.label: Say you got out of bed today
choices.title: A standing achievement
choices.result: The facilitator calls this a triumph over horizontal thinking. Everyone stands to applaud. You sit down before they can invent a course about it.
choices.journal: I told a motivational group that getting out of bed was my achievement.

choices.label: Ask what the investigations were about
choices.title: We celebrate, we do not enquire
choices.result: The facilitator rings a tiny bell and announces a positivity break. The person beside you quietly moves their bag farther away from the previous speaker.
choices.journal: I derailed a motivational introduction by asking about eight workplace investigations.

choices.label: Claim you invented motivational seminars
choices.title: The founder gets a leaflet
choices.result: The facilitator asks why you are attending a taster session. You say you are checking on the franchise. They give you a leaflet and personally show you out.
choices.journal: I claimed to have invented motivational seminars and was shown out of one.

events.reason: Overediting a greeting generated no external incident or specific consequence.

before.title: The message before the message
before.body: You begin writing a reply, delete it, write another and then notice that you have spent longer on the greeting than the conversation deserves.

choices.label: Send a simple, clear reply
choices.title: A perfectly ordinary message
choices.result: The reply communicates what you meant. Nobody requests a more elegant opening.
choices.journal: I stopped polishing a message and sent a clear reply.

choices.label: Put it aside and return later
choices.title: A little distance helps
choices.result: When you return, the sentence looks much less important. You find the words more easily.
choices.journal: I took a break from overthinking a short message.

choices.label: Continue refining every word
choices.title: A greeting with a full workday
choices.result: You produce several excellent versions of hello. The actual reply remains unwritten.
choices.journal: I spent too long editing the beginning of a simple message.

after.title: Discreet volunteers wanted
after.body: You post a request for cleanup volunteers in a community chat. Your phone attaches an old shopping list: bleach, bin bags and cable ties. Someone replies, “What exactly are we cleaning?”

choices.label: Explain that it is a garden cleanup
choices.title: The photographs help
choices.result: You attach a photo of weeds and broken plant pots. Two people volunteer. A third asks for a picture of you holding today’s newspaper. You decline that part.
choices.journal: I explained a suspicious shopping list attached to my garden-cleanup request.

choices.label: Delete the post without explaining
choices.title: A screenshot is forever
choices.result: Someone immediately reposts a screenshot asking why you deleted it. You explain the garden. They reply with a thumbs-up that somehow feels worse.
choices.journal: I made a suspicious community-chat message worse by deleting it.

choices.label: Add “No questions. Bring gloves.”
choices.title: One clarification too many
choices.result: The moderator turns off replies and calls you. You spend twelve minutes describing bindweed to a person who now knows far too much about your afternoon.
choices.journal: I made a harmless cleanup request sound worse and had to explain it to the chat moderator.

events.reason: Incorrect lyrics led to generic participation versus pedantry.

before.title: A chorus everyone almost knows
before.body: At a free neighbourhood singalong, everyone confidently starts the chorus and then disagrees about the second line.

choices.label: Laugh and follow the group
choices.title: Several versions, one chorus
choices.result: The song keeps going. Accuracy becomes less important than the effort everyone is making together.
choices.journal: I joined a singalong whose lyrics had several local editions.

choices.label: Listen until the next familiar line
choices.title: An honest musical pause
choices.result: You return when you know the words. Listening does not disqualify you from the afternoon.
choices.journal: I enjoyed a singalong without pretending to know every lyric.

choices.label: Stop to correct every version
choices.title: A rehearsal nobody booked
choices.result: The group loses its place while you establish the official wording. The chorus never asked for an editor.
choices.journal: I interrupted a singalong to argue about its words.

after.title: The song of extra garlic
after.body: At a community singalong, the lyric projector fails. It starts displaying a takeaway receipt instead. The backing track continues. Everyone looks to you for the first line.

choices.label: Sing the receipt with feeling
choices.title: Hold the onions
choices.result: You hit the high note on “extra garlic”. The room joins in for “delivery instructions”. The organiser finally switches off the projector during the sauce options.
choices.journal: I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

choices.label: Pass the microphone down the row
choices.title: A duet with customer service
choices.result: The next singer performs the restaurant’s telephone number. Someone recognises the tune and orders dinner before the music ends.
choices.journal: I passed on a singalong microphone while the screen displayed a takeaway receipt.

choices.label: Demand that they restore the proper words
choices.title: The crowd has chosen
choices.result: The organiser finds the lyrics. The room boos and demands the receipt back. You spend the final chorus refusing to sing about complimentary bread.
choices.journal: I tried to restore the lyrics after a singalong became a takeaway order.

choices.result: You flatten it and clear the area. The hypothetical need for this exact box remains hypothetical.

choices.result: The cupboard closes with some persuasion. Your future box requirements are comprehensively covered.

after.body: An anonymous parcel arrives at home. Inside is a glitter bomb that works perfectly. A note says, “Think about what you did.” You cannot narrow it down.

choices.label: Pay {money} for a professional cleanup
choices.title: A specialist in your mistake
choices.result: The cleaner charges {money} and asks whether to save the note. You say no. They remove most of the glitter. One fleck survives on the bin lid, shining like a threat.
choices.journal: I paid {money} to clean up an anonymous glitter bomb.

choices.label: Turn it into an accidental craft afternoon
choices.title: Festive evidence
choices.result: You make three greeting cards and a deeply unpleasant bookmark. The glitter is now on four additional surfaces. You put the cards away before choosing recipients.

choices.result: You send the photo to people who might know. Three reply “Wasn’t me” before you ask a question. One asks whether it worked. Nobody admits anything.

events.reason: A window smudge had no surprise; replaced with an accidental sneeze in a neighbouring property advert. The playful branch shares the image in a chat, with no claim that a saved avatar or account picture changed.

before.title: The view has a smudge

choices.label: Clean the small patch
choices.title: The bird disappears

choices.journal: I removed a window smudge that had looked like a distant bird.

choices.label: Add it to your next tidy-up

choices.result: You note the job and return to what you were doing. Recognising a task does not require doing it instantly.

choices.title: The culprit is flat
choices.result: You switch it off and find the bath mat plastered across the drum. You add a few towels and restart it. The machine stays put. The bath mat has lost its transport.

choices.label: Accompany it on an empty laundry basket

choices.label: Brace it in place until the cycle ends

choices.result: You spend eight minutes pushing against the machine. It finishes with a cheerful tune. You hang the bath mat up, then sit down on the floor beside the perfectly good chair.
choices.journal: I exhausted myself holding a badly loaded washing machine in place until its cycle ended.

before.title: Every result uses a louder font

choices.label: Write the question down and close the page

choices.label: Find out who wrote the article

choices.label: Keep clicking until it tells you something

events.reason: Vague unsupported-advice discussion becomes a fraudulent trained-potato cure, with real optional spending and no invented recovery.

choices.journal: I asked for evidence behind a claimed cure for {condition}.

choices.label: Argue until they admit uncertainty

choices.result: The conversation consumes your patience without settling the claim. You decide it can end without agreement.
choices.journal: I spent too long debating unsolicited advice about {condition}.

after.title: The potato has a doctorate
after.body: An acquaintance claims they can cure your {condition}. Their method involves a specially trained potato. You ask what training a potato receives. They say that is proprietary.

choices.label: Say you will wait for a peer-reviewed vegetable
choices.title: The potato is unavailable for questions
choices.result: They offer to remove the sprouts at no extra charge. You end the conversation before discussing the postgraduate options.
choices.journal: I declined a supposed potato cure for {condition}.

choices.label: Ask to see the potato’s qualifications
choices.title: Doctor is an honorary title
choices.result: The certificate names the Institute of Natural Possibilities. The signature is printed in the same handwriting as the price.
choices.journal: I questioned the credentials behind a ridiculous potato cure for {condition}.

choices.label: Buy the supposed cure — {money}
choices.title: A very expensive potato
choices.result: You pay {money} and receive one potato with a card saying Believe. No instructions, no treatment. It starts sprouting before your faith does.
choices.journal: I lost {money} buying a bogus potato cure for {condition}.

events.reason: Uses a visibly edited influencer week to make the comparison tangible. Humour targets the production, with distinct disengage, question-list and anxious-replay endings.

choices.journal: I stopped comparing my experience of {condition} with an influencer’s edited week.

events.reason: Generic autoplay lesson becomes an accidental fitness-video challenge with gentle, seated and genuinely costly overreach outcomes.

before.title: The next episode has already started
before.body: You intended to stop watching a programme, but the next episode begins before you have decided whether to stand up.

choices.journal: I stopped watching when I had planned to stop.

choices.label: Choose one more deliberately
choices.title: A choice with a clear ending
choices.result: You decide to enjoy one more episode and set a definite stopping point. The decision feels better when it is actually yours.
choices.journal: I deliberately chose one more episode and a clear stopping point.

choices.label: Let the programme choose for you
choices.title: Several endings later
choices.result: More episodes finish. You feel less rested than you expected from sitting still for so long.
choices.journal: I kept watching after I stopped making a real choice about it.

after.title: The sofa is judging you
after.body: Autoplay follows your programme with a competitive fitness class. A man who appears to have been assembled entirely from elbows challenges you to beat your personal best.

choices.label: Switch to the beginner version and try it
choices.title: An achievable number of elbows
choices.result: You complete the gentler routine. The instructor says anyone can do it, then folds himself into a shape you decline to investigate.
choices.journal: I followed a beginner workout after a fitness video appeared on autoplay.

choices.label: Invent a chair-based version
choices.title: Advanced sitting
choices.result: You lift your feet whenever he jumps and call it low-impact training. By the cooldown, you have become extremely good at remaining seated.
choices.journal: I invented an extremely seated version of a workout video.

choices.label: Keep up with him at full speed
choices.title: The floor is your cooldown partner
choices.result: The third burpee makes you yelp. You finish lying under the table while the instructor asks whether you would like a harder challenge.
choices.journal: I overdid a demanding workout video and finished in pain under the table.

events.reason: Turns posture advice into a disputed chair creak, with different physical actions and aftermaths rather than a movement lesson.

before.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
before.body: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Take a gentle movement break
choices.title: A different position helps
choices.result: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.
choices.journal: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

choices.label: Change your position and relax your shoulders
choices.title: Less unnecessary effort
choices.result: You notice how tightly you were holding yourself and make a small adjustment.
choices.journal: I adjusted my position when I noticed tension in my shoulders.

choices.label: Stay exactly as you are
choices.title: The complaint remains open
choices.result: You keep going without changing position. The tension continues asking for your attention.
choices.journal: I ignored tension from sitting in the same position.

after.title: The chair denies everything
after.body: After sitting still for ages, you stand halfway up and hear a tremendous creak. You and the chair are the only suspects.

choices.label: Take a short victory lap
choices.title: The investigation gets some air
choices.result: You walk around until you feel less stiff. On your return, you give the chair a suspicious look. It refuses to demonstrate the noise.
choices.journal: I loosened up with a short walk after a creak of uncertain origin.

choices.label: Rearrange yourself like an expensive display
choices.title: A better seating arrangement
choices.result: You shift your feet, lower your shoulders and settle back. The chair gives one small squeak. You are delighted to have a witness.
choices.journal: I adjusted my sitting position and let the chair take the blame for the noises.

choices.label: Remain completely still to protect your alibi
choices.title: A difficult position to defend
choices.result: Nothing creaks because nothing moves. Unfortunately, your shoulders have begun objecting in ways the chair cannot be blamed for.
choices.journal: I stayed stiff rather than investigate a suspicious creak.

before.title: The quiet place has noises
before.body: You sit somewhere quiet and immediately notice a clock, a distant door and somebody clearing their throat. Apparently quiet did not mean perfectly silent.

choices.title: Quiet enough is available
choices.result: You stop checking each sound for a reason to be irritated. The place becomes restful without becoming silent.
choices.journal: I accepted ordinary background sounds in a quiet moment.

choices.label: Choose one steady sound to notice
choices.title: A smaller field of attention
choices.result: You listen for a while without judging the whole room. The other noises become less demanding.
choices.journal: I focused on one steady sound instead of monitoring every noise.

choices.label: Identify every interruption
choices.title: A complete catalogue of noises
choices.result: Your list becomes impressively detailed. Rest receives rather less attention than the clock.
choices.journal: I spent a quiet moment cataloguing everything that interrupted it.

after.title: The silence committee
after.body: In a library’s quiet corner, someone whispers “Shh.” Another person shushes them for shushing too loudly. A third has taken a preparatory breath.

choices.label: Read while the committee meets
choices.title: The dispute has excellent acoustics
choices.result: You settle into your book. Behind you, two people attempt to win an argument entirely through the letter S.
choices.journal: I relaxed with a book while other readers argued about making less noise.

choices.label: Listen to the clock instead
choices.title: One participant keeps good time
choices.result: You follow the steady ticking. When the shushing pauses, you realise you have been tapping along. You very quietly stop.
choices.journal: I focused on a clock rather than a dispute in the library’s quiet corner.

choices.label: Ask who started it
choices.title: A unanimous decision
choices.result: All three turn towards you and say “Shh.” You have united the room and become its newest problem.
choices.journal: I interrupted an argument about silence and got shushed by everyone involved.

before.title: A minute without filling it
before.body: You have a short wait with nothing to do. Before reaching for a distraction, you notice you have already checked the same screen three times.

choices.label: Look around for a minute
choices.title: The world supplies a few details
choices.result: You notice a small sign and an interesting pattern of light. The wait becomes a moment rather than a gap to erase.
choices.journal: I spent a short wait noticing what was around me.

choices.label: Let your attention rest
choices.title: A pause without a job
choices.result: You let the minute pass without giving it a task. Waiting remains waiting and feels less demanding.
choices.journal: I let a short wait stay unfilled.

choices.label: Check the same screen again
choices.title: No new material
choices.result: The screen looks much as it did a moment ago. You continue looking for something to make the wait disappear.
choices.journal: I refreshed a screen that had nothing new to show me.

after.title: Assistance is a trap
after.body: In a waiting area, a bell sits between two signs: RING FOR ASSISTANCE and PLEASE DO NOT RING. You have already checked your phone three times.

choices.label: Look for a third opinion
choices.title: Help is apparently nearby
choices.result: You spot WE ARE HERE TO HELP above a firmly closed hatch. Studying the signs turns out to be more interesting than your phone.
choices.journal: I passed a wait investigating contradictory reception signs.

choices.label: Close your eyes and let someone else decide
choices.title: A brave volunteer

choices.label: Refresh the same screen again

events.reason: Turns generic productivity pressure into an overambitious planner; finishing three tasks, enjoying a book and exhausting yourself have distinct endings.

before.title: You must make the most of it
before.body: You feel better rested than usual and immediately begin planning enough tasks to use every available bit of energy.

choices.label: Choose a few priorities and leave room
choices.title: A useful day with an ending
choices.result: You use some energy without treating all of it as a resource that must be exhausted.
choices.journal: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

choices.label: Enjoy feeling well without a quota
choices.title: A good moment can simply count
choices.result: You allow yourself to notice the easier feeling. It does not have to produce proof that it was deserved.
choices.journal: I enjoyed feeling rested without turning it into a productivity target.

choices.label: Fill every bit of the day
choices.title: The full capacity gets used
choices.result: You accomplish several things and finish drained. Feeling rested did not make your energy unlimited.
choices.journal: I used up a good day by treating it as an obligation to do everything.

after.title: Fix your life before lunch
after.body: You wake up feeling rested. Your planner suggests clearing your inbox, learning a language and becoming an entirely new person. It has left twenty minutes for lunch.

choices.label: Pick three manageable tasks and mute the planner

choices.result: You finish your three tasks and stop. The planner suggests setting an ambitious new target. You suggest it enjoys the silence.
choices.journal: I finished three manageable tasks and muted an overambitious planner.

choices.label: Spend some of this energy enjoying yourself
choices.title: No measurable improvement
choices.result: You read for pleasure without timing it. Nobody becomes their best self, and you have a lovely afternoon.
choices.journal: I enjoyed a rested afternoon instead of turning it into a productivity project.

choices.label: Attempt the entire recommended new personality
choices.title: The inbox is a different person
choices.result: You clear your inbox and keep adding tasks until you are exhausted. The planner congratulates you and asks what you are doing tomorrow.
choices.journal: I wore myself out trying to complete an overambitious day’s plan.

events.reason: Uses a one-sentence journal and an absurdly dramatic resignation to show three different reactions to a missed day.

choices.label: Write today’s sentence and carry on
choices.title: The dog retains top billing

choices.journal: I resumed a one-sentence journal after missing a day.

events.reason: Replaces irritation advice with a nosy question about tiredness. A questionnaire joke, short break and needless insult produce different reactions.

before.title: Before answering immediately
before.body: A mildly irritating question arrives while you are already tired. You notice the sharp reply forming before the other person has finished speaking.

choices.label: Take a moment before answering
choices.title: A reply with less edge
choices.result: The pause gives you time to separate the question from your tiredness. You answer the thing that was actually asked.
choices.journal: I paused before answering sharply when I was tired.

choices.label: Say you need a short break
choices.title: A clearer limit
choices.result: You explain that your patience is running low and return to the question after a moment.
choices.journal: I asked for a short break instead of replying through irritation.

choices.label: Deliver the sharp reply
choices.title: Now there are two problems
choices.result: The question remains, accompanied by an argument about your tone. Tiredness has not become easier to manage.
choices.journal: I snapped at a small question because I was tired.

after.title: Customer support is unavailable
after.body: You are tired when someone asks, “Why do you look so tired?” They wait as though you have been withholding an exciting explanation.

choices.label: Ask whether the survey has a second question
choices.title: A limited questionnaire
choices.result: They ask whether you have been sleeping enough. You request an unsubscribe button. They laugh and change the subject.
choices.journal: I joked my way out of questions about looking tired.

choices.label: Say you will answer after a short break
choices.title: The explanation can wait
choices.result: You take a quiet break. When you return, they have forgotten the question. You decide against reopening the investigation.
choices.journal: I took a short break instead of answering an irritating question while tired.

choices.label: Ask why their face looks like that
choices.title: A follow-up nobody wanted
choices.result: They demand to know what is wrong with their face. You are now tired and trying to explain that you did not have a specific objection.
choices.journal: I turned a question about looking tired into an argument by insulting someone.

before.title: The set list has become art
before.body: You look over a handwritten set list and realise one title could equally be a song, a weather warning or an instruction to leave the room.

choices.label: Rewrite the unclear titles plainly
choices.title: A more readable performance plan
choices.result: The list becomes useful again. Attractive handwriting is allowed to come second to knowing what comes next.
choices.journal: I made an unclear set list readable.

choices.label: Check the intended order before guessing
choices.title: A small clarification
choices.result: You confirm the title and sequence. The potential weather warning turns out to be a song after all.
choices.journal: I clarified a confusing title in a set list.

choices.label: Trust your most dramatic interpretation
choices.title: An unnecessary private plot twist
choices.result: You prepare for an order nobody else intended. Looking at the list again would have been quicker.
choices.journal: I guessed at a set list instead of checking it.

after.title: The crowd knows your shopping list
after.body: At a small public performance, your lyric screen displays your shopping list. The front row is already chanting “bin bags”. You have not reached the chorus.

choices.label: Sing the list as written
choices.title: A surprisingly strong bridge
choices.result: You give “large onions” everything you have. The crowd joins in. By the final bin bag, people are applauding an arrangement you sincerely hope never to repeat.
choices.journal: I turned an accidentally displayed shopping list into a crowd singalong.

choices.label: Explain the mistake and play without lyrics
choices.title: Requests politely refused
choices.result: You close the list and carry on from memory. Somebody requests washing-up liquid. You decline with enough dignity to finish the set.
choices.journal: I recovered a public performance after displaying my shopping list instead of lyrics.

choices.label: Accuse them of leaking your new material
choices.title: The bootleg includes carrots
choices.result: You demand to know who stole the lyrics. Someone holds up a supermarket receipt. The laughter follows you all the way through the next song.
choices.journal: I accused an audience of piracy after accidentally showing them my shopping list.

before.title: Dress appropriately
before.body: Your service preparation note says “PT, then formal”. You cannot tell whether you need training kit, formal clothes or the confidence to combine them.

choices.label: Ask before assembling the outfit
choices.title: A question saves a silhouette
choices.result: You confirm what to wear and when. Your imagined outfit would have answered neither question correctly.
choices.journal: I clarified clothing instructions during service preparation.

choices.label: Check the current preparation list
choices.title: Two entries, in order
choices.result: The full list separates the activities. It turns out the uniform was not intended to be a collage.
choices.journal: I checked the full service preparation list before dressing.

choices.label: Practise the combined look in the mirror
choices.title: Ready for absolutely nothing
choices.result: You try formal clothes with training shorts. The reflection suggests a person fleeing two different events.
choices.journal: I bluffed my way through unclear service preparation instructions.

after.title: Inspection by fragrance
after.body: You discover someone has labelled a bottle of shoe polish “aftershave”. You notice just before using it. Your service kit now smells of a very shiny conspiracy.

choices.label: Check every bottle before using anything
choices.title: A kit with trust issues
choices.result: You find soap labelled “emergency cheese”. You restore the labels and finish preparing. Whoever arranged this has put more work into the joke than the kit.
choices.journal: I checked and restored misleading labels on my service preparation kit.

choices.label: Ask the room who smells of footwear
choices.title: The witness has polished cheeks
choices.result: One person touches their face and immediately regrets it. You hand over a cloth. The investigation ends without needing a confession.
choices.journal: I exposed a service-kit labelling prank by asking who had used the shoe polish.

choices.label: Polish one boot with your real aftershave
choices.title: Excellent scent, terrible finish
choices.result: You use your real aftershave. Your boot smells expensive and looks greasy. You spend the rest of preparation removing it. The correctly labelled polish watches from the shelf.
choices.journal: I used my real aftershave on a boot to retaliate against a service-kit labelling prank.

events.reason: Replace generic acronym advice with a public conspiracy question and actual public-image effects.

before.title: No acronyms this time
before.body: In a space-programme discussion, you are asked to explain a technical idea without using acronyms. Your first sentence contains three.

choices.label: Start with what the system does
choices.title: An explanation with a clear starting point
choices.result: You describe the purpose before the labels. The technical detail becomes easier to place.
choices.journal: I explained a space-programme idea without relying on acronyms.

choices.label: Try a careful everyday comparison

choices.result: The comparison gives people a starting point. You also explain where it stops matching the real system.
choices.journal: I used a careful comparison to explain a technical idea.

choices.label: Spell out every acronym at full length
choices.title: Longer words, same problem
choices.result: The expanded names remain unexplained. You have complied with the lettering rule while missing the point.
choices.journal: I replaced acronyms with long names instead of explaining their meaning.

after.title: The Earth question
after.body: At a public space-programme question session, a man asks whether the Earth is flat. He has brought a spirit level. The microphone is already pointed at you.

choices.label: Explain what the level actually measures
choices.title: A locally flat demonstration
choices.result: You level the table, then explain why the whole planet does not fit on it. Several people laugh. The man checks the table again, just to be sure.
choices.journal: I answered a flat-Earth question by explaining a visitor’s spirit level.

choices.label: Use an orange to show the difference
choices.title: A difficult piece of fruit
choices.result: You balance the level against the orange. The man says fruit is different. You agree that this is the first uncontested fact of the session.
choices.journal: I used an orange to explain the Earth’s shape during a public space-programme session.

choices.label: Tell him the level is part of the cover-up
choices.title: An official source, regrettably
choices.result: He thanks you for confirming it. Your explanation that this was sarcasm gets less attention than your original answer. You can hear the phones recording.
choices.journal: I made a conspiracy joke at a public space-programme session and was taken literally.

events.reason: Replace ribbon untangling with a false donation announcement; optional personal donation really costs money.

before.title: The ribbon has two beginnings
before.body: At a public ceremonial preparation, two ribbons have been folded together so neatly that nobody can find which end is supposed to be presented first.

choices.label: Wait while the organiser separates them
choices.title: A ceremony returns to its instructions
choices.result: You allow a small delay without making it a personal crisis. The ribbons eventually agree to become two ribbons.
choices.journal: I waited patiently through a small ceremonial ribbon mix-up.

choices.label: Make a gentle joke about the preparation
choices.title: The room relaxes a little
choices.result: The joke gives the organiser a moment without making them its target. The preparation continues.
choices.journal: I eased a ceremonial delay without embarrassing the organiser.

choices.label: Demand to know who is responsible
choices.title: An inquiry larger than the ribbon
choices.result: Several people become tense while the original practical problem remains exactly the same size.
choices.journal: I made a ceremonial ribbon problem into an unnecessary confrontation.

after.title: Sponsored scissors
after.body: At a charity ribbon-cutting, the organiser announces that you have personally sponsored the scissors. This is news to you. Cameras turn towards the scissors, then your face.

choices.label: Correct the claim before cutting anything
choices.title: A donor with no donation
choices.result: You explain that you agreed to cut the ribbon, not fund the equipment. The organiser corrects the announcement. The scissors remain perfectly usable without your endorsement.
choices.journal: I corrected a charity organiser who announced a donation I had not made.

choices.label: Donate {money} of your own money
choices.title: Scissors, officially sponsored
choices.result: You make the {money} donation and cut the ribbon. The organiser offers you the scissors to keep. You ask them to get more than one use out of the investment.
choices.journal: I donated {money} from my own funds after being announced as the scissors’ sponsor.

choices.label: Dedicate the scissors to yourself
choices.title: A moving tribute to the donor
choices.result: Without promising money, you request a minute’s silence for your generosity. The organiser lowers the microphone. The cameras do not lower theirs.
choices.journal: I mocked a false donation announcement by dedicating the charity scissors to myself.

choices.result: You give {pet} a little time to respond and move together at an easier pace.
choices.journal: I patiently encouraged {pet} to leave an interesting smell behind.

choices.label: Keep impatiently calling their name
choices.title: The name gets a lot of use
choices.result: {pet} looks between you and the ground. You have made a small pause feel unnecessarily urgent.
choices.journal: I grew impatient while {pet} investigated a smell.

after.title: The gnome is a suspect
after.body: On a walk, {pet} plants all four paws in front of a garden gnome and growls. The gnome is smiling in a way that does seem provocative.

choices.label: Allow a formal investigation
choices.title: The village elder is cleared
choices.result: {pet} sniffs the gnome, checks behind it and leaves. The suspect maintains exactly the same expression.
choices.journal: I waited while {pet} investigated a suspicious garden gnome.

choices.label: Introduce them properly
choices.title: A meeting of garden dignitaries
choices.result: You explain that the gnome is made of concrete. {pet} sniffs it and moves on before you can discuss its occupation.
choices.journal: I introduced {pet} to a garden gnome to get our walk moving again.

choices.label: Announce that the gnome is your new dog
choices.title: The existing dog objects
choices.result: {pet} nudges your hand, then stands between you and the gnome. You apologise to a dog while a small concrete man watches.
choices.journal: I upset {pet} by pretending a garden gnome was their replacement.
