before.title: The packaging is the attraction
before.body: {pet} ignores a clear space you made and settles beside an empty box instead. Your interior design has received a concise review.

choices.label: Let them choose the safe spot
choices.title: The review is accepted
choices.result: You check that the space is safe and let {pet} enjoy it. The preferred arrangement was apparently very simple.
choices.journal: I accepted {pet}’s preference for an ordinary box.

choices.label: Watch what makes the spot appealing
choices.title: A useful bit of attention
choices.result: You notice the sheltered angle and quiet corner. {pet} has provided a lesson without agreeing to teach one.
choices.journal: I paid attention to the kind of space {pet} preferred.

choices.label: Keep rearranging everything around them
choices.title: The room becomes a moving target
choices.result: {pet} leaves to find a quieter place. Your effort has outgrown the reason for it.
choices.journal: I kept disturbing {pet} while trying to improve their chosen spot.

after.title: The cardboard heir
after.body: You save a box for {pet}. They move into its lid, which is barely big enough to contain their dignity. The larger box stands empty like an unsold mansion.

choices.label: Declare the lid a luxury studio
choices.title: One occupant, excellent ventilation
choices.result: You add a paper sign advertising city views and a private cat. {pet} sleeps through the viewing.
choices.journal: I advertised {pet}’s tiny cardboard lid as luxury accommodation.

choices.label: Try the big box yourself
choices.title: The second cat is rejected
choices.result: You get one foot inside. {pet} watches from the lid. You withdraw your application to share the accommodation.
choices.journal: I tried fitting into the box {pet} had rejected.

choices.label: Keep upgrading the lid with cardboard walls
choices.title: An abandoned development
choices.result: By the third wall, {pet} has moved into the big box. You finish an extension for an empty lid.
choices.journal: I overbuilt {pet}’s favourite cardboard spot until they moved out.

events.reason: Shows species-appropriate blinking, voluntary rubbing and withdrawal through a mock interview, without explaining the correct attitude.

before.title: A very small conversation
before.body: {pet} watches you from a comfortable distance and slowly closes their eyes. You realise how easy it would be to turn a calm moment into an interruption.

choices.label: Stay quiet and let them approach
choices.title: Company on their terms
choices.result: You leave the distance for {pet} to choose. The quiet feels companionable without requiring a performance.
choices.journal: I enjoyed calm company with {pet} without demanding attention.

choices.label: Offer gentle attention if they want it
choices.title: An invitation with room to decline
choices.result: You keep the invitation small. {pet} can come closer or remain comfortably where they are.
choices.journal: I let {pet} choose whether to come closer.

choices.label: Call repeatedly until they react
choices.title: The quiet moment leaves first
choices.result: {pet} looks away. You have succeeded in getting a reaction at the expense of the calm you noticed.
choices.journal: I interrupted a calm moment by repeatedly calling {pet}.

after.title: The interview is over
after.body: {pet} sits opposite you, studies your face and slowly closes their eyes. You feel as though you have applied for a position and the panel is still deciding.

choices.label: Blink back and wait for the decision
choices.title: You may remain on the premises
choices.result: {pet} stretches out nearby and shuts their eyes again. You stay quietly together. The interview appears to have become a nap.
choices.journal: I quietly returned {pet}’s slow blink and kept them company.

choices.label: Offer one finger for inspection
choices.title: References accepted
choices.result: {pet} sniffs your finger, then rubs against your hand. You provide the requested attention without asking about the salary.
choices.journal: I let {pet} approach and gave them the attention they asked for.

choices.label: Keep calling the panel by name
choices.title: No further correspondence
choices.result: {pet} gets up, turns away and sits facing the wall. You have received a decision in a very clear format.
choices.journal: I spoiled a calm moment with {pet} by repeatedly calling for their attention.

events.reason: Gives the rabbit an interesting slipper and lets approach, observation and crowding produce concrete, species-appropriate reactions.

before.title: A different height of conversation
before.body: {pet} watches cautiously while you stand nearby. From down there, you probably look like a very large interruption.

choices.label: Sit quietly at a comfortable distance
choices.title: The room becomes less imposing
choices.result: You give {pet} time to decide how close to come. The small approach feels better because it was not forced.
choices.journal: I sat quietly and let {pet} choose the distance.

choices.label: Give them space and observe
choices.title: Attention without crowding
choices.result: You notice what makes {pet} comfortable and leave the space around them calm.
choices.journal: I paid attention to {pet}’s comfort without crowding them.

choices.label: Keep reaching in for attention
choices.title: The invitation feels too large
choices.result: {pet} moves away. Wanting a friendly moment did not make it useful to insist on one.
choices.journal: I crowded {pet} when they wanted more space.

after.title: The ground-floor inspection
after.body: {pet} is investigating a slipper while you try to attract their attention. From floor level, the slipper appears to be the more promising acquaintance.

choices.label: Sit on the floor and await inspection
choices.title: Almost as interesting as footwear
choices.result: {pet} approaches and nudges your hand. You keep still while they investigate. The slipper has some competition at last.
choices.journal: I sat quietly and let {pet} approach me.

choices.label: Watch the slipper investigation from a distance
choices.title: An extremely thorough tenant
choices.result: {pet} checks the opening, circles the heel and checks the opening again. You enjoy the inspection without interrupting it.
choices.journal: I gave {pet} space and watched them investigate a slipper.

choices.label: Keep reaching over to introduce yourself
choices.title: The viewing is over
choices.result: {pet} moves just beyond your fingertips and returns to the slipper. You have somehow lost a social contest to an empty shoe.
choices.journal: I kept reaching towards {pet} when they wanted more space.

events.reason: Species-specific vocal interruption and three distinct reactions.

before.title: A devastating second opinion
before.body: You finish practising an impressive introduction aloud. {pet} responds with a noise so much like a fart that you lose your place.

choices.label: Thank them for the editorial feedback
choices.title: An accessible review format
choices.result: {pet} repeats the noise. You practise a shorter introduction while trying not to laugh.
choices.journal: I laughed at {pet} interrupting my introduction practice.

choices.label: Wait quietly for the critic to finish
choices.title: No further notes
choices.result: {pet} settles down. You restart without the grand opening.
choices.journal: I calmly waited out {pet}’s noisy interruption.

choices.label: Deliver the introduction at full volume
choices.title: Two terrible speeches
choices.result: {pet} gets louder too. Nobody in the room is becoming more impressive.
choices.journal: I tried to outshout {pet} during a noisy moment.

events.reason: Replaces abstract companionship with a confidential briefing to a pet. Results remain suitable for every supported species and preserve the real pet-bond changes.

before.title: Someone else is in the room
before.body: You have been absorbed in your own thoughts when you notice {pet} nearby. Their ordinary presence makes the room feel less empty.

choices.label: Spend a quiet moment together
choices.title: Ordinary company counts
choices.result: You put your attention on {pet} for a while. The moment does not need to become a more elaborate activity.
choices.journal: I enjoyed a quiet moment of company with {pet}.

choices.label: Notice how they seem to be feeling
choices.title: A little more attention
choices.result: You watch their behaviour without rushing to interpret every movement. Familiarity still has things to teach you.
choices.journal: I paid closer attention to {pet}’s ordinary behaviour.

choices.label: Stay too distracted to respond
choices.title: The moment passes quietly
choices.result: You return to your thoughts. {pet} remains part of the room without receiving much of your attention.
choices.journal: I let a chance for quiet company with {pet} pass.

after.title: A confidential briefing
after.body: You have been telling {pet} about your day. You reach “You had to be there” before remembering who your audience is.

choices.label: Settle down and tell the short version
choices.title: An excellent listener
choices.result: You talk quietly for a while and feel less wound up. {pet} offers no unsolicited advice. You thank them for their professionalism.
choices.journal: I relaxed while keeping {pet} company and talking about my day.

choices.label: Pause to see what interests your audience
choices.title: The interview turns around
choices.result: You stop narrating and watch {pet} go about their usual business. For once, you let someone else provide the entertainment.
choices.journal: I stopped talking long enough to pay attention to {pet}.

choices.label: Check your phone halfway through your own story
choices.title: The speaker has lost interest
choices.result: You disappear into your screen. When you remember {pet}, you cannot even recall the point of the story you abandoned.
choices.journal: I missed a chance to spend time with {pet} by getting distracted by my phone.

events.reason: Generic attention lesson becomes a full-name disciplinary hearing for the named pet.

before.title: The important sound is your voice
before.body: You say {pet}’s name in a gentle voice and notice a small change in their attention. Familiar sounds have become part of living together.

choices.label: Give them a little warm attention
choices.title: A familiar exchange
choices.result: You keep the interaction calm and brief. {pet} gets your attention without having to compete for it.
choices.journal: I gave {pet} a warm moment of attention.

choices.label: Wait for their response
choices.title: Their own pace
choices.result: You let the response arrive when it arrives. A small connection does not need to become a test.
choices.journal: I waited patiently for {pet} to respond to me.

choices.label: Repeat the name as a constant test
choices.title: A name becomes background noise
choices.result: You keep asking for a reaction until the exchange loses its gentleness. You can hear the impatience in your own voice.
choices.journal: I turned {pet}’s response to their name into an unnecessary test.

after.title: The pet has your surname
after.body: You catch yourself giving {pet} your surname during a stern speech. Apparently you are now the headteacher of a school with one pupil.

choices.label: Apologise and offer some attention
choices.title: The hearing ends on the floor
choices.result: {pet} accepts the attention. You finish the disciplinary hearing on the floor, using the silliest voice you possess.
choices.journal: I abandoned a stern lecture and gave {pet} some attention.

choices.label: Ask the pupil to explain their actions
choices.title: A consistent defence
choices.result: {pet} pauses, then resumes exactly what they were doing. The defence rests without changing its position.
choices.journal: I jokingly asked {pet} to explain themselves.

choices.label: Continue the full-name lecture
choices.title: The pupil is elsewhere
choices.result: You reach “This household has rules” and hear how you sound. {pet} has been studying an entirely different part of the room.
choices.journal: I gave {pet} a long lecture they had no interest in hearing.

events.reason: A small haunted-room mystery with insect, companionship and landlord payoffs.

before.title: The corner has a visitor
before.body: {pet} stares at an empty corner, slowly turns to look at you, and returns to staring. You were enjoying not wondering whether the room was haunted.

choices.label: Check what they are watching
choices.title: The haunting has six legs
choices.result: A tiny insect moves along the wall. {pet} appears disappointed that you needed help noticing it.
choices.journal: I found the insect {pet} was watching.

choices.label: Sit beside them and investigate together
choices.title: Two detectives, limited progress
choices.result: You spend a quiet minute watching the corner with {pet}. Whatever it is, it has your combined attention.
choices.journal: I kept {pet} company during an investigation of a corner.

choices.label: Loudly announce that ghosts must pay rent
choices.title: One tenant leaves immediately
choices.result: {pet} walks away from the noise. The corner gives no reply to your property policy.
choices.journal: I disturbed {pet} by shouting at an empty corner.

after.title: The corner has a visitor
after.body: {pet} stares at an empty corner, slowly turns to look at you, and returns to staring. You were enjoying not wondering whether the room was haunted.

choices.title: One tenant leaves immediately
choices.result: {pet} walks away from the noise. The corner gives no reply to your property policy.
choices.journal: I disturbed {pet} by shouting at an empty corner.

events.reason: Generic pattern-recognition lesson becomes self-supplied hold music, with three distinct performances and a real modest music gain.

before.title: The chord knows another song
before.body: After guitar practice, you notice that a familiar chord sequence sounds like several songs you know. Your fingers appear to have joined a very large club.

choices.label: Listen for what makes the songs different
choices.title: The same starting point goes places
choices.result: You notice the rhythm and melody doing different jobs. The familiar chords become more interesting rather than less.
choices.journal: I noticed how different songs used a familiar guitar sequence.

choices.label: Enjoy recognising the connection
choices.title: A small moment of recognition
choices.result: You let the connection be enjoyable without turning it into a test of how many songs you can identify.
choices.journal: I enjoyed recognising a familiar guitar pattern.

choices.label: Decide every song is the same now
choices.title: A very small theory of music
choices.result: The conclusion feels clever for a moment. It leaves out most of what you liked listening to.
choices.journal: I dismissed too much music after recognising one shared pattern.

after.title: Please hold for your guitar solo
after.body: During guitar practice, you recognise your new three-chord masterpiece. It is the hold music from a company that once kept you waiting for forty minutes.

choices.label: Give the hold music a dramatic solo
choices.title: Your complaint has a guitar solo
choices.result: You miss a note and announce that all agents are currently busy. The next attempt sounds annoyingly good.
choices.journal: I turned some familiar hold music into a guitar solo.

choices.label: Perform it like a stadium anthem
choices.title: Forty thousand people awaiting refunds
choices.result: You bow to an imaginary crowd. In your head, the entire stadium has been told their call is important.
choices.journal: I performed hold music as an imaginary stadium anthem.

choices.label: Tell everyone you composed it
choices.title: A familiar body of work
choices.result: Someone hums the next note before you play it. You claim they must have heard your earlier material.
choices.journal: I claimed some recognisable hold music was my own composition.

events.reason: Specific ridiculous artwork, distinct plausible reactions and a complete visual punchline.

before.title: A difficult portrait
before.body: You turn your practice painting sideways. The dignified landscape now looks exactly like a furious bottom with a moustache.

choices.label: Study how you accidentally painted that
choices.title: An educational bottom
choices.result: Once you see it, the moustache is impossible to ignore. You learn a lot about shapes and very little about dignity.
choices.journal: I studied an accidental face in my practice painting.

choices.label: Keep it sideways and give it a serious title
choices.title: Portrait of an Important Man
choices.result: The title makes it worse in exactly the way you hoped. You keep your favourite mistake.
choices.journal: I kept a ridiculous accidental version of my painting.

choices.label: Insist this is precisely what you intended
choices.title: A bold artistic statement
choices.result: Explaining the moustache requires several new lies. It was easier when the picture was simply bad.
choices.journal: I pretended an embarrassing painting was deliberate.

events.reason: Photography lesson becomes an admired image of the photographer’s own thumb; each response gives a concrete visual payoff.

before.title: The background has a leading role
before.body: Reviewing photographs from practice, you notice that your favourite frame includes a bin positioned as though it were an important monument.

choices.label: Look at how the background changes it
choices.title: The whole frame matters
choices.result: You understand why your eye keeps returning to the bin. The observation gives you something specific to notice next time.
choices.journal: I studied an unintentionally prominent background in a practice photo.

choices.label: Keep the funny practice frame
choices.title: A monument to paying attention
choices.result: You enjoy the accidental composition. A practice photo is allowed to make you laugh as well as teach you something.
choices.journal: I enjoyed a practice photograph whose background stole the scene.

choices.label: Blame the camera for including it
choices.title: The camera records your objection poorly
choices.result: The frame stays exactly as you composed it. Your complaint does not make the background less visible.
choices.journal: I blamed my practice photograph on the camera.

after.title: A masterpiece by your thumb
after.body: Your best practice photograph is a glowing, mysterious landscape. After several minutes of admiration, you realise it is your finger covering most of the lens.

choices.label: Recreate it on purpose
choices.title: The artist is attached
choices.result: You try three exposures and discover that your thumb has a better side. The rest of your hand remains ordinary.
choices.journal: I deliberately recreated an accidental photograph of my thumb.

choices.label: Call it The Human Condition
choices.title: An intensely personal work
choices.result: Someone says the image feels very personal. You agree. It is still attached to you.
choices.journal: I gave a photograph of my thumb a very serious title.

choices.label: Accuse the camera of censorship
choices.title: The equipment responds
choices.result: You wipe the lens and take a perfectly clear photograph of the floor. The camera appears to have a strong defence.
choices.journal: I blamed my camera for a photograph I had taken with my finger over the lens.

events.reason: Concrete chess blunder and distinct excuse, review and admiration payoffs.

before.title: Checkmate, apparently
before.body: Reviewing a practice chess game, you discover that your brilliant queen sacrifice was just leaving your queen where it could be eaten.

choices.label: Find the move that would have saved her
choices.title: Her Majesty had options
choices.result: There were six safe squares. You write down the useful part before counting them again makes you angry.
choices.journal: I reviewed a disastrous queen move from chess practice.

choices.label: Admire how quickly your opponent noticed
choices.title: A generous donation
choices.result: You can laugh at the disaster now. Your opponent required less time to appreciate it.
choices.journal: I laughed at an opponent punishing my chess mistake.

choices.label: Describe it as an advanced psychological trap
choices.title: The trap caught somebody
choices.result: Your explanation lasts longer than the rest of the game did. The queen remains unavailable for comment.
choices.journal: I made excuses for losing my queen during chess practice.

events.reason: Memorable absurd mystery reveal with a different joke in each response.

before.title: The butler was a horse
before.body: The mystery you read ends by revealing that the murderer was a horse in a butler costume. You turn back to see whether you missed something extremely important.

choices.label: Look for hoofprints in the earlier chapters
choices.title: The clues were offensively literal
choices.result: The butler refused stairs, adored apples and “answered with a lengthy snort.” You owe the book an apology.
choices.journal: I found the clues to a ridiculous mystery ending.

choices.label: Write a spoiler-free review of this outrage
choices.title: Difficult to discuss without neighing
choices.result: You settle on “the staff behave unusually.” Leaving out the twist takes more restraint than finishing the book.
choices.journal: I wrote a restrained review of a bizarre mystery ending.

choices.label: Spoil it in every reading discussion you enter
choices.title: The only mystery is why you are still talking
choices.result: You make sure nobody else gets surprised. Several people had been looking forward to that.
choices.journal: I spoiled a mystery ending for other readers.

events.reason: Repeated read-the-instructions lesson becomes exposure of a ridiculous old username and three different attempts at damage control.

before.title: The tip arrives after the mistake
before.body: Remembering a practice game, you realise the loading-screen tip explained the exact mistake you made five minutes later. Apparently it was not just decoration.

choices.label: Keep the useful part for next time
choices.title: Advice finally reaches its destination
choices.result: You understand why the tip mattered after seeing the situation. One clear lesson is enough to take away.
choices.journal: I connected a gaming tip with a mistake from practice.

choices.label: Laugh at the timing
choices.title: The game did try to tell you
choices.result: You enjoy the gap between seeing the words and understanding them. The mistake becomes a better story than an excuse.
choices.journal: I laughed at missing advice a game had already given me.

choices.label: Insist the game never explained anything
choices.title: The evidence waits on the next loading screen
choices.result: The same tip appears again. It remains inconveniently relevant to your complaint.
choices.journal: I blamed a game for advice I had overlooked.

after.title: Long live the Toilet King
after.body: A practice game displays your old username: Supreme_Toilet_King. It sits directly above a notice asking players to behave respectfully.

choices.label: Rename yourself SomethingProfessional
choices.title: The position is already filled
choices.result: SomethingProfessional is taken. You settle for SomethingProfessional2 and quietly resent your predecessor.
choices.journal: I replaced an embarrassing gaming name with SomethingProfessional2.

choices.label: Keep it. The crown fits.
choices.title: A royal announcement
choices.result: You introduce yourself in chat as Your Majesty. Someone asks whether the throne has a flush. You concede that it does.
choices.journal: I embraced my ridiculous old gaming username.

choices.label: Insist it is an ancient family title
choices.title: A question of succession
choices.result: The chat requests your coat of arms. You leave before anyone starts designing it.
choices.journal: I pretended my embarrassing gaming name was a noble family title.

events.reason: Patience lecture becomes a collapsed cake; salvage, celebration and concealment produce different disasters.

before.title: Allow to cool before touching
before.body: Looking back at a supervised cooking session, you remember reading “allow to cool” just after becoming very eager to see how the result turned out.

choices.label: Make patience part of the recipe
choices.title: The waiting is an instruction too
choices.result: You recognise that the quiet steps matter as much as the busy ones. The lesson is clearer now that the excitement has passed.
choices.journal: I noticed why a cooking recipe included time to cool.

choices.label: Enjoy the story of your impatience
choices.title: An impatient cook meets a timer
choices.result: You remember how slowly the final minutes seemed to pass. The result was not improved by watching it more intensely.
choices.journal: I laughed at how impatient I had been during cooking practice.

choices.label: Decide waiting instructions are optional
choices.title: A recipe loses a useful step
choices.result: You defend the shortcut more strongly than the result deserves. The written instruction still has a reason for being there.
choices.journal: I dismissed the value of waiting during cooking practice.

after.title: The cake needs an alibi
after.body: Your cooking-practice cake refuses to leave the tin. You turn it over. The middle lands on the plate; the edge remains a structural part of the pan.

choices.label: Serve it in bowls as a new dessert
choices.title: Deconstructed, under pressure
choices.result: You call it deconstructed cake. People ask for seconds. Nobody asks where the construction went.
choices.journal: I rescued a collapsed practice cake by serving it as a dessert in bowls.

choices.label: Give the wreckage a birthday anyway
choices.title: A moving ceremony
choices.result: You sing to the heap of crumbs. Blowing out the imaginary candle scatters the guest of honour across the table.
choices.journal: I sang Happy Birthday to the remains of a cake.

choices.label: Put it back together and ice over the evidence
choices.title: The cover-up is unstable
choices.result: The first slice moves sideways before the knife touches it. Your icing has created a small landslide.
choices.journal: I tried to hide a collapsed cake under icing.

events.reason: Keeps the strong mistaken-weed premise and gives Gary a label correction, an expanding family and a fictional heritage garden as distinct payoffs.

before.title: The weed got a name
before.body: Looking back at gardening practice, you realise you carefully labelled a weed and ignored the actual plant. You even complimented its progress.

choices.label: Check the leaves and correct your notes
choices.title: A promising career in weeds
choices.result: The difference is obvious once you know what to look for. You record it without the encouraging speech.
choices.journal: I corrected a plant identification mistake after gardening practice.

choices.label: Learn to recognise your former star pupil
choices.title: Congratulations withdrawn
choices.result: You study the leaf shape. At least next time you will know exactly what you are praising.
choices.journal: I learned to recognise a weed I had mistaken for a plant.

choices.label: Decide the weed deserves your loyalty
choices.title: It believed in you too
choices.result: You defend the label rather than correct it. Your gardening notes are becoming a work of fiction.
choices.journal: I refused to correct a wrong plant label in my gardening notes.

after.title: Gary is thriving
after.body: During gardening practice, you realise the thriving plant you labelled GARY is a weed. The actual plant is much smaller and has received none of your encouraging speeches.

choices.label: Correct the label and check the actual plant
choices.title: A difficult change of management
choices.result: You relabel Gary as WEED and tend the neglected plant. Your notes now say “Check the leaves before naming anyone.”
choices.journal: I corrected a weed’s label and paid attention to the plant I meant to grow.

choices.label: Study what made Gary so convincing
choices.title: There are more of him

choices.label: Write down the detail before losing it
choices.title: More than a date remains
choices.result: You keep a short description of what the ticket reminded you of. The memory now has a little more context.
choices.journal: I wrote down a detail I remembered about {destination}.

choices.label: Dismiss it and keep sorting
choices.title: The date returns to being a date
choices.result: You put the paper aside and continue. The remembered detail slips back out of attention.
choices.journal: I passed over an old reminder of {destination}.

after.title: The refund of the century
after.body: Among your souvenirs from {destination}, you find a claim form for a duplicate booking charge. A stamp on the back says APPROVED. Your most valuable holiday memory might be a clerk’s handwriting.

choices.label: Claim the refund — receive {money}
choices.title: The souvenir pays out
choices.result: The {money} refund reaches your account. Your postcard from {destination} said memories last forever. Apparently departmental queues do too.
choices.journal: I claimed a {money} refund for a duplicate booking charge from my trip to {destination}.

choices.label: Frame the approved form instead
choices.title: A rare administrative beauty
choices.result: You display it beside a photograph from {destination}. Visitors admire the stamp. You never get round to claiming the actual money.

choices.label: Shred it with the junk mail
choices.title: Approved for confetti
choices.result: Halfway through the first strip, you spot the approval stamp. The paperwork from {destination} now looks suitable for a very small parade.
choices.journal: I accidentally shredded an approved travel refund form from {destination}.

events.reason: Folding lesson becomes a bogus souvenir map with three concrete ways of exposing or embracing its fabricated geography.

before.title: The map no longer folds that way
before.body: A paper map kept from {destination} opens easily enough. Returning it to its original shape appears to require knowledge not printed on the map.

choices.label: Follow the old creases patiently
choices.title: A modest folding achievement
choices.result: You work through the creases without forcing them. The map eventually resembles a map rather than a geography-themed parcel.
choices.journal: I patiently folded an old map from {destination}.

choices.label: Give it a simpler practical fold
choices.title: A different route to the same drawer
choices.result: It fits neatly enough. The original fold is allowed to remain one of the journey’s mysteries.
choices.journal: I found a practical new fold for a map from {destination}.

choices.label: Force it until the corners agree
choices.title: Several additional corners appear
choices.result: The map becomes bulkier as your certainty increases. It has discovered a new shape without discovering agreement.
choices.journal: I argued physically with an old map from {destination}.

after.title: Officialish Tourism
after.body: Your souvenir map of {destination} labels three areas YOU ARE HERE, DEFINITELY NOT HERE and ASK SOMEONE ELSE. The stall that sold it was called Officialish Tourism.

choices.label: Compare it with a real map
choices.title: A bold interpretation of geography
choices.result: A museum is in a river. An important road is missing. You draw one accurate route: from the souvenir map to the bin.
choices.journal: I discovered that my souvenir map of {destination} was mostly invented.

choices.label: Keep it as modern art
choices.title: Geography improves upside down
choices.result: You hang it upside down. The geography is hardly worse, and the big blob now resembles a heroic rat.
choices.journal: I turned an inaccurate map of {destination} into wall art.

choices.label: Complain to the address printed on the back
choices.title: The map supplies directions
choices.result: The address reads Large tree, near the middle. You stare at it for a full minute. It includes a helpful arrow pointing off the paper.
choices.journal: I tried to complain about a bogus map of {destination} using its equally bogus address.

events.reason: Personal-record lesson becomes an automatically generated holiday film dominated by food and a chin, with three distinct edits/reactions.

before.title: A remarkably well-documented lunch
before.body: Looking through reminders of {destination}, you notice that an ordinary meal seems to have received more attention than a famous view.

choices.label: Enjoy what you actually noticed
choices.title: Your attention had its own itinerary
choices.result: You remember the moment around the meal. A personal record does not have to resemble a brochure.
choices.journal: I enjoyed an ordinary food memory from {destination}.

choices.label: Describe the detail beyond the plate
choices.title: The memory has more room
choices.result: You recall the surroundings and how the day felt. The meal turns out to have been a useful marker for the whole moment.
choices.journal: I remembered the setting around a meal in {destination}.

choices.label: Decide you documented the trip incorrectly
choices.title: A retrospective photography assignment
choices.result: You judge old choices by a list you did not have at the time. The memory becomes less enjoyable without becoming more accurate.
choices.journal: I criticised the way I had remembered my trip to {destination}.

after.title: A journey of nine sandwiches
after.body: Your phone makes a highlight video of {destination}: twenty-three meals, one sunset and a close-up of your chin. It titles the film A Journey of Discovery.

choices.label: Show the director’s cut
choices.title: The chin has screen presence
choices.result: Your audience watches nine consecutive sandwiches before asking whether you left the restaurant. The chin receives the best review.
choices.journal: I showed an accidentally food-dominated highlight video of {destination}.

choices.label: Re-edit it as a cooking documentary
choices.title: Soup changes everything
choices.result: Your narration calls a bowl of soup a turning point. The sunset is cut for pacing.
choices.journal: I turned my food photos from {destination} into a mock cooking documentary.

choices.label: Defend every single meal photo
choices.title: An important variation in toast
choices.result: You explain why the second piece of toast deserved its own shot. Everyone has noticed the exit except you.
choices.journal: I bored people defending every meal photo from {destination}.

events.reason: Turns an abstract holiday habit into a local walk mistaken for being lost, with useful directions or a self-defeating pavement review.

before.title: Something you did differently there
before.body: You remember a simple habit you enjoyed during your completed visit to {destination}: slowing down long enough to notice where you were.

choices.label: Try a brief version close to home

choices.result: You take an unhurried look at an ordinary place nearby. The useful part of the memory fits into a small moment.
choices.journal: I brought a little of my slower pace in {destination} into an ordinary day.

choices.label: Think about what made it easier there
choices.title: A clearer reason for the memory
choices.result: You notice the different expectations you had while away. Understanding them is more useful than demanding that every day feel like a trip.
choices.journal: I considered why I had slowed down more easily in {destination}.

choices.label: Expect the whole day to feel like a holiday
choices.title: An ordinary day receives an unfair brief
choices.result: The day continues containing ordinary responsibilities. The memory was offering a small idea, not a complete replacement.
choices.journal: I compared an ordinary day unfairly with my time in {destination}.

after.title: The local scenic route
after.body: You try bringing home the slow walks you enjoyed in {destination}. A neighbour spots you looking around and asks whether you are lost.

choices.label: Explain that you are walking without a goal
choices.title: Directions are supplied anyway
choices.result: They point down the road just in case. You thank them and continue enjoying a walk that has apparently become suspicious.
choices.journal: I enjoyed a slow walk inspired by {destination}, despite being mistaken for someone lost.

choices.label: Ask where they go for a pleasant walk
choices.title: An unexpected local recommendation
choices.result: They think hard, then point to a quiet little street you usually hurry past. You make a note of it. Your hometown has acquired a tiny itinerary.
choices.journal: I asked for a local walking suggestion after remembering my slower pace in {destination}.

choices.label: Explain that the walks were better in {destination}
choices.title: A demanding review of a pavement
choices.result: They suggest trying the next street. You continue comparing every ordinary corner with your holiday and enjoy none of them.
choices.journal: I spoiled a local walk by insisting it should feel like my visit to {destination}.

events.reason: Balanced-review lesson becomes an actual friend’s unauthorised public guarantee, with meaningful bond and trust fallout.

before.title: “Was it worth going?”
before.body: {friend} asks what you thought of {destination}. You notice how quickly a real experience can become a demand for a single rating.

choices.journal: I gave {friend} a balanced account of my visit to {destination}.

choices.label: Explain what made it worthwhile for you
choices.title: A personal answer stays personal
choices.result: You describe what mattered to you without promising that everyone would feel the same.
choices.journal: I told {friend} what I personally valued about {destination}.

choices.label: Declare that everyone must go
choices.title: A recommendation with no room in it
choices.result: {friend} asks whether you considered that people want different things from a trip.
choices.journal: I treated my opinion of {destination} as a requirement for everyone.

after.title: Five stars, no permission
after.body: {friend} asks for your honest verdict on {destination}. They are recommending it publicly and have already put your name under A PERSONAL GUARANTEE. Nobody asked you for one.

choices.label: Give them the honest version
choices.title: Paradise receives amendments
choices.result: You mention the crowds as well as the view. {friend} deletes paradise from the draft and asks whether lovely, eventually would be fair.
choices.journal: I helped {friend} write an honest recommendation of {destination}.

choices.label: Insist they remove your name
choices.title: Your name is not a coupon code
choices.result: {friend} says it was just marketing. You ask why the marketing has your name on it. They delete the guarantee.
choices.journal: I made {friend} remove my name from an unauthorised guarantee about {destination}.

choices.label: Publicly comment: I guaranteed none of this
choices.title: The review loses its guarantor
choices.result: {friend} deletes the post, then asks why you did not message them privately. You send a screenshot of their guarantee. They leave it on read.
choices.journal: I publicly challenged {friend} for using my name to guarantee a trip to {destination}.

events.reason: Makes the changed plans a memorable free button exhibition; enthusiasm, a balanced retelling and an inflated disaster story resolve differently.

before.title: The weather declined the brochure
before.body: You remember a day in {destination} when the weather changed your plans. The part you still talk about was not on the original itinerary.

choices.label: Remember the alternative you found
choices.title: A different good memory
choices.result: You recall the decision you made after the plan changed. The detour has become part of why you remember the day.
choices.journal: I remembered how I adapted to changed plans in {destination}.

choices.label: Let the disappointment and enjoyment coexist
choices.title: The whole day gets to stay
choices.result: You keep both parts of the memory. An enjoyable ending does not require pretending the original disappointment never happened.
choices.journal: I let a mixed memory of {destination} stay mixed.

choices.label: Retell it as an entirely ruined day
choices.title: The story loses its better half
choices.result: You leave out the part you ended up enjoying. The stronger complaint makes the memory less true.
choices.journal: I exaggerated a weather-disrupted day in {destination} into a complete disaster.

after.title: An emergency interest in buttons
after.body: Rain in {destination} once drove you into a free exhibition about buttons. Your photo is captioned Highlight of the day. You are not entirely sure you were being sarcastic.

choices.label: Take another look at the button photos
choices.title: The ceremonial one holds up
choices.result: You enlarge a photograph of a particularly grand button. It really was impressive. You spend a cheerful minute remembering a day the brochure failed to predict.
choices.journal: I enjoyed remembering an unexpected button exhibition during a rainy day in {destination}.

choices.label: Admit the weather was awful and the buttons excellent
choices.title: An oddly persuasive travel story
choices.result: Your listener starts by laughing, then asks to see the ceremonial button. You explain that it was considerably larger than the everyday ones.
choices.journal: I told the whole story of a rainy day and an unexpectedly enjoyable exhibition in {destination}.

choices.label: Retell it as a brush with death

choices.result: You call the exhibition an emergency shelter. Someone asks why your best photograph from the disaster is a nicely lit button.
choices.journal: I exaggerated a wet day in {destination} until my own photographs undermined the story.

events.reason: Lets the actual friend impose a timer. A trailer, a three-word exchange and an endless suitcase explanation give concrete friendship payoffs.

choices.journal: I shared one short memory of {destination} with {friend}.

choices.journal: I asked what {friend} wanted to know about {destination}.

choices.journal: I gave {friend} a much longer account of {destination} than they asked for.

choices.journal: I corrected a stranger’s assumption about my daily life.

choices.label: Say the birds are frightened of you
choices.title: A more demanding hobby
choices.result: You explain that you watch them to maintain order. The stranger laughs and finally asks a real question.
choices.journal: I joked about birdwatching after a stranger made assumptions about my age.

choices.label: Describe every activity they failed to imagine
choices.title: An unexpectedly busy conversation
choices.result: You list so much that they begin glancing at the time. You have proved you can fill an afternoon, including theirs.
choices.journal: I gave a long lecture to someone who assumed my days were empty.

events.reason: Generic kindness-to-younger-self lesson becomes a confident old demand for wealth and fitted-sheet mastery.

before.title: You recognise the handwriting
before.body: You find an old note in your own handwriting. The letters are familiar, but the urgent little instruction belongs to a version of you with different worries.

choices.label: Read it with a little kindness
choices.title: A person doing their best then
choices.result: You remember the circumstances without judging them by what you know now. The old worry seems easier to understand.
choices.journal: I read an old note to myself with more kindness than criticism.

choices.label: Write what you understand differently now
choices.title: Two versions of the same person
choices.result: You put a short present-day thought beside the old instruction. Neither has to pretend to know the other’s whole life.
choices.journal: I wrote a present-day thought beside an old note.

choices.label: Scold the old version of yourself
choices.title: A verdict delivered very late
choices.result: You criticise an old uncertainty using information that person did not have. It does little for either version of you.
choices.journal: I judged an old worry too harshly with the benefit of hindsight.

after.title: A complaint from your younger self
after.body: You find a note from your younger self: By fifty-five, we will be independently wealthy and know how to fold a fitted sheet. The handwriting is extremely confident.

choices.label: Write back about the sheet
choices.title: The corners remain hostile
choices.result: You report that the elastic corners remain a problem. You omit finances; you are not being interrogated by a child with a felt-tip pen.
choices.journal: I answered an old note about being wealthy and folding fitted sheets.

choices.label: List what you did achieve
choices.title: An amended list of demands
choices.result: The list gets longer. You finish with Bought my own bed linen and underline it twice.
choices.journal: I answered an unrealistic old note with a list of what I had actually achieved.

choices.label: Send your younger self a furious reply
choices.title: An awkward chain of command
choices.result: You call them financially illiterate and bad at deadlines. Then you remember where all their decisions ended up.
choices.journal: I wrote an angry reply to my younger self’s unrealistic plans.

events.reason: Replaces anxiety commentary with scissors, an intrusive advertising jingle and an out-of-service number. No illness or decline is invented.

before.title: A number with nowhere to go
before.body: You suddenly remember a telephone number you have not used for years. You cannot remember what you entered a room to fetch, but the number is perfect.

choices.label: Enjoy the memory’s strange priorities
choices.title: An impressive useless recital
choices.result: You repeat the number once and laugh at the timing. Memory has supplied an answer to a question nobody asked.
choices.journal: I remembered an old telephone number at an unhelpful moment.

choices.label: Return calmly to the original task
choices.title: One thought at a time
choices.result: You retrace what you were doing instead of treating the distraction as an emergency.
choices.journal: I calmly retraced a small task after an odd memory interrupted it.

choices.label: Treat the distraction as a personal crisis
choices.title: A small lapse gets a large audience
choices.result: Worry fills the space where a simple pause might have helped. The old number remains unreasonably easy to remember.
choices.journal: I worried too much about a small distraction.

after.title: The number will not leave
after.body: You are looking for scissors when an old television jingle pops into your head, complete with its telephone number. Your memory has supplied a service nobody requested.

choices.label: Sing the jingle while you search
choices.title: An impressive advertising legacy
choices.result: You find the scissors halfway through the second chorus. You have never been less grateful to a catchy tune.
choices.journal: I found the scissors while singing an old advertising jingle I still remembered perfectly.

choices.label: Write the number down and retrace your steps
choices.title: The notepad had the answer
choices.result: You write down the number, then lift the notepad to put it away. The scissors are underneath. Neither service required a telephone call.
choices.journal: I found missing scissors under the notepad I used to get an old number out of my head.

choices.label: Ring the number and demand answers
choices.title: Customer services has left the century
choices.result: A recording says the number is out of service. The scissors have still not provided a statement.
choices.journal: I wasted time calling an old advertising number instead of finding the scissors.

events.reason: Concrete slang misunderstanding with distinct responses and a natural reveal.

before.title: Apparently you ate
before.body: A younger person points at your outfit and says, “You ate.” You have no food on you. They add, “No crumbs.” This is getting less clear.

choices.label: Ask whether this is a compliment
choices.title: Breakfast has nothing to do with it
choices.result: It is a compliment. You thank them and ask for a translation before anyone says anything else about your digestion.
choices.journal: I asked someone to explain a slang compliment about my outfit.

choices.label: Reply, “Thank you. It was delicious.”
choices.title: Fluent enough
choices.result: They laugh and explain the phrase. You insist you knew that. Your pause before “phrase” does you no favours.
choices.journal: I joked through an unfamiliar compliment and learned what it meant.

choices.label: Announce that you can feed yourself
choices.title: An unnecessary declaration of independence
choices.result: You deliver a speech about patronising older people. Halfway through, someone quietly explains the compliment.
choices.journal: I mistook a slang compliment for a comment on my ability to eat.

events.reason: Abstract perspective lesson becomes a dispute with a card-game app that produces its own rulebook; no additional participant gate.

before.title: You can still explain the rules
before.body: A casual mention of an old game reminds you of a disputed result from years ago. You can still present the entire case with alarming precision.

choices.label: Tell it as a funny old argument
choices.title: The result loses its jurisdiction
choices.result: You enjoy how much the dispute once mattered without reopening it as a current legal matter.
choices.journal: I laughed about a game dispute that used to feel very important.

choices.label: Notice how the stakes have changed
choices.title: A smaller trophy in memory
choices.result: You remember the feeling and recognise its old scale. The memory can stay vivid without staying urgent.
choices.journal: I put an old competitive argument into perspective.

choices.label: Present the case as though still pending
choices.title: The appeal enters another decade
choices.result: You make a detailed argument to an audience with no power to alter the result.
choices.journal: I reopened an old game dispute in unnecessary detail.

after.title: The final appeal
after.body: A card-game app informs you that you have been playing an old favourite incorrectly for decades. You dispute this. The rectangle produces a rulebook.

choices.label: Invent a house rule and silence the app
choices.title: A local variation
choices.result: You mute the little victory tune until it stops judging you. You then award yourself a win under a rule added thirty seconds ago.
choices.journal: I invented a house rule after a card-game app challenged the way I played.

choices.label: Learn the proper rule and play one game
choices.title: A technically magnificent defeat
choices.result: You lose correctly for the first time in your life. It is less thrilling than the tutorial suggested.
choices.journal: I learned the proper rules of an old card game and promptly lost.

choices.label: Read every rule for a loophole
choices.title: The case is suspended
choices.result: You find a notice saying the app needs to restart after an update. You close it and concede nothing.
choices.journal: I hunted through a card game’s rules before using an update notice as an excuse to quit.

events.reason: Gives the old photo a paper hat and urgent gesture, with an honest caption, a cake discovery and an implausible spy story as distinct endings.

before.title: You are almost in the picture
before.body: An old photograph catches you at the edge of the frame, apparently concentrating on something outside it. You can no longer remember what seemed so important.

choices.label: Enjoy the unfinished little mystery
choices.title: A life outside the frame
choices.result: You let the unknown detail remain unknown. The photograph still holds an ordinary moment worth keeping.
choices.journal: I enjoyed an old photograph without solving every detail.

choices.label: Write down what you do remember
choices.title: Some details stay
choices.result: You record the clear parts without inventing an explanation for the rest.
choices.journal: I preserved the details I actually remembered from an old photograph.

choices.label: Build a grand explanation around the pose
choices.title: A very ambitious caption
choices.result: You produce a story much more dramatic than the picture supports. It is entertaining as long as you remember it is a guess.
choices.journal: I invented an elaborate explanation for an old photograph.

after.title: A significant gesture
after.body: An old group photo catches you leaning out of frame and pointing urgently at something. Everyone is wearing paper party hats. You look as though you are trying to alter the course of history.

choices.label: Keep it as proof you were mostly present
choices.title: An accurate historical record
choices.result: You caption it “Present, with reservations.” It becomes your favourite description of a party you can barely remember.
choices.journal: I gave an old party photo an honest caption instead of solving its mystery.

choices.label: Look through the rest of the photographs
choices.title: The urgency returns
choices.result: The next shot shows someone carrying away the last slice of cake. Suddenly you remember exactly what mattered that day.
choices.journal: I discovered that my urgent gesture in an old photo concerned the last slice of cake.

choices.label: Explain that you were giving a secret signal
choices.title: The disguise needs work
choices.result: Your account reaches “covert operation” before someone asks about the paper hat. You call it undercover attire. They stop asking about the mission.
choices.journal: I invented a secret mission to explain an odd pose in an old party photograph.

events.reason: Makes the autonomy question a stubborn jar, so accepting, politely trying a cloth and snapping all have tangible reactions without an age-based judgement.

before.title: Help has been offered
before.body: Someone offers a hand with a small practical task. You are not sure you need the help, but you notice yourself preparing a defence before considering the offer.

choices.label: Accept if the help would be useful
choices.title: A task shared
choices.result: You take the useful part of the offer without treating it as a judgement on everything you can do.
choices.journal: I accepted useful help with a small task.

choices.label: Politely decline and explain your preference
choices.title: A clear answer is enough
choices.result: They accept your answer. You keep your independence without having to turn kindness into an argument.
choices.journal: I declined an offer of help politely.

choices.label: Treat the offer as an insult
choices.title: The task gains an argument
choices.result: The person withdraws the offer. You have defended your independence at the expense of an ordinary friendly exchange.
choices.journal: I reacted harshly to a well-meant offer of help.

after.title: The lid is winning
after.body: You are struggling with a stubborn jar when someone offers to help. The lid has already survived your polite request and your less polite one.

choices.label: Let them have a go
choices.title: A shared enemy
choices.result: They give it a confident twist. Nothing. You both agree the lid is unreasonable and keep trying together.
choices.journal: I accepted help with a stubborn jar and gained an ally against the lid.

choices.label: Politely try a tea towel first
choices.title: There was a system
choices.result: The lid finally gives. You explain that you had a system. They ask whether glaring at it for two minutes was part of the system.
choices.journal: I politely declined help and got a stubborn jar open with a tea towel.

choices.label: Deliver a speech about unsolicited assistance
choices.title: An extremely independent jar
choices.result: They leave you to it. You announce “I can open a jar!” to a lid that is currently disproving you.
choices.journal: I snapped at someone offering help and stayed stuck with a stubborn jar.

events.reason: Repeated bucket gag gives each response a concrete object and payoff.

before.title: It cannot have been this bad
before.body: You revisit a comedy you have called your favourite for years. Ten minutes in, a man falls into a bucket for the fourth time. You appear to have remembered a much better programme.

choices.label: Admit your taste has improved
choices.title: The bucket loses a fan
choices.result: You stop watching without trying to defend your younger self in court. There are other ways to spend the evening.
choices.journal: I stopped pretending to enjoy an old favourite programme.

choices.label: Work out what you used to enjoy
choices.title: It may have been the company
choices.result: You remember the circumstances around the programme more clearly than the jokes. The bucket was doing less work than you thought.
choices.journal: I considered why an old favourite no longer appealed to me.

choices.label: Watch the whole thing out of loyalty
choices.title: Nine buckets later
choices.result: You defend the pacing to an empty room. By the credits, the bucket has received more screen time than the supporting cast.
choices.journal: I sat through an old favourite that I no longer enjoyed.

events.reason: Uses a documentary’s grand description of a remote control to give familiarity, explanation and offended arithmetic their own payoffs.

before.title: The programme is now retro
before.body: A recording you remember as ordinary entertainment is introduced as a fascinating example of a past era. The past era appears to have included your evenings.

choices.label: Enjoy noticing what has changed
choices.title: An accidental historical perspective
choices.result: You spot details that once passed unnoticed. Familiarity gives you another way to watch it.
choices.journal: I enjoyed seeing an old programme presented as a period piece.

choices.label: Describe one detail you remember clearly
choices.title: A small first-hand footnote
choices.result: You add a useful detail without trying to speak for everyone who was there.
choices.journal: I shared a specific memory of something now described as retro.

choices.label: Object to the entire concept of retro
choices.title: The era continues being earlier than now
choices.result: The label remains on the recording. Your objection has not moved the calendar backwards.
choices.journal: I took a retro label more personally than it deserved.

after.title: The domestic command device
after.body: A documentary uses a programme you remember watching as “historical footage”. The narrator earnestly introduces its remote control as an early domestic command device.

choices.label: Watch your ordinary evenings become history
choices.title: An important era for channel changing
choices.result: You enjoy spotting details the narrator misses. Apparently the little lid that always fell off the remote was not important enough for the archives.
choices.journal: I enjoyed a documentary treating a familiar old programme as historical footage.

choices.label: Explain what the remote actually did
choices.title: An expert is consulted
choices.result: You describe changing channels. Someone asks why it needed four buttons marked AV. You had been hoping nobody would ask.
choices.journal: I explained an old remote control while avoiding questions about its more mysterious buttons.

choices.label: Object to calling any of this historical
choices.title: The narrator brings dates
choices.result: You insist it was not that long ago. The narrator announces the year. You begin an argument with their arithmetic.
choices.journal: I argued with a documentary for calling a familiar programme historical footage.

events.reason: A bland birthday conversation becomes a cake with an extra zero and several different uses of ancient status.

before.title: Another year, by the calendar
before.body: Someone asks how you feel about another birthday and seems to expect a complaint. Your actual answer is a little less tidy than that.

choices.label: Give the mixed, honest answer
choices.title: More than a familiar complaint
choices.result: You name something you value and something you find difficult. The answer feels more like your life than a ready-made line.
choices.journal: I gave an honest answer about another birthday.

choices.label: Mention one ordinary thing you enjoy now
choices.title: A small present-day reason
choices.result: You choose a detail that matters to you. It is enough for this conversation without becoming a verdict on every year.
choices.journal: I noticed something ordinary I enjoy at my current age.

choices.label: Deliver the complaint they seem to expect
choices.title: A well-rehearsed answer
choices.result: The line gets the expected response. It leaves rather less room for what you actually feel.
choices.journal: I answered a birthday question with a complaint that was not the whole truth.

after.title: Older than bread
after.body: A birthday cake for you arrives with an extra zero among the candles. Someone asks whether you knew the person who invented bread.

choices.label: Ask for the extra candles to be removed
choices.title: A breakthrough in reverse ageing
choices.result: They remove the extra candles, then stand back as though they have made you younger. You thank the bakery for its medical breakthrough.
choices.journal: I corrected an extra zero on my birthday cake.

choices.label: Keep the cake and accept your ancient status
choices.title: A respected elder claims the icing
choices.result: You refer to the fridge as the ice chest and demand a seat near the fire. The extra icing tastes like power.
choices.journal: I embraced an exaggerated age on my birthday cake and ate the evidence.

choices.label: Deliver a speech about surviving the last ice age
choices.title: The ancient one has the floor
choices.result: You blame the price of butter on the fall of civilisation. Somebody takes away the cake knife until the speech is over.
choices.journal: I turned a birthday cake mistake into a very long speech about being ancient.

events.reason: Strong original pigeon-poo/art-interpretation reversal with distinct reactions.

before.title: The loneliness of pigeon poo
before.body: A free photography exhibition features you under the title “The Loneliness of Age”. In the photo, you are staring at the pavement. You remember trying not to step in pigeon poo.

choices.label: Listen to the visitors analyse your pain
choices.title: A moving interpretation of a dirty pavement
choices.result: Someone praises your quiet despair. You sit down to enjoy the discussion of what was actually a difficult pavement crossing.
choices.journal: I listened to visitors misinterpret a candid photo of me at an exhibition.

choices.label: Tell the photographer what you were looking at
choices.title: The artist has questions
choices.result: The photographer asks whether the pigeon poo could represent something. You explain that it represented a problem for your shoes.
choices.journal: I explained the unglamorous context of an exhibition photo of me.

choices.label: Offer a live performance of your suffering
choices.title: The subject refuses to be profound
choices.result: You demonstrate dodging imaginary droppings beside the photograph. A visitor laughs; the photographer asks you to stop improving the exhibition.
choices.journal: I mocked an overly solemn interpretation of a photograph by reenacting it.

events.reason: Specific low-stakes rebellion, consistent free activity and a satisfying failed revolution.

before.title: The underground number game
before.body: At a free games afternoon, the caller bans shouting “Bingo!” until every number has been checked. A player beside you whispers that this is how dictatorships begin.

choices.label: Check your numbers and play along
choices.title: Order survives another round
choices.result: You finish a peaceful game while the rebellion beside you struggles to remember whether they heard forty-six.
choices.journal: I followed the rules at a contentious free games afternoon.

choices.label: Ask the rebel about their resistance plans
choices.title: The movement needs stationery
choices.result: They propose a rival afternoon with fewer rules and better biscuits. You enjoy the conversation without signing up for anything.
choices.journal: I joked with a disgruntled player about rebelling against game rules.

choices.label: Shout “Bingo!” with an empty card
choices.title: A revolution with no numbers
choices.result: The room falls silent while the caller inspects your card. Your rebellion ends under twenty separate disappointed stares.
choices.journal: I interrupted a free games afternoon with a deliberately false bingo call.

events.reason: Concrete salary context, a real coworker and three already distinct social outcomes.

before.title: Show me yours
before.body: {coworker} asks your salary while standing beneath a poster saying “We are one big family”. Your annual gross pay is {salary}. This family has secrets.

choices.label: Tell them the actual figure
choices.title: The family learns a number
choices.result: {coworker} goes very quiet, then thanks you for being honest. Neither of you looks at the poster.
choices.journal: I told {coworker} my annual gross pay was {salary}.

choices.label: Demand to hear theirs first
choices.title: Two very private people
choices.result: {coworker} suddenly remembers something else to do. You both keep your numbers and a little suspicion.
choices.journal: I kept my salary private and asked {coworker} to reveal theirs first.

choices.label: Add a zero. Act exhausted.
choices.title: A lie with impressive overheads
choices.result: {coworker} asks why you keep complaining about money. You discover that inventing wealth requires further invention.
choices.journal: I exaggerated my salary to {coworker}.

events.reason: Replace the evasive handover with a malicious ranking, both real workplace roles, and trust/performance consequences.

before.title: Nothing to report
before.body: {coworker}’s handover says, “Everything was normal. If anyone asks, you saw nothing.” You were hoping for instructions rather than an alibi.

choices.label: Ask exactly what you supposedly did not see
choices.title: A much smaller mystery
choices.result: The alarming secret is a task they forgot to finish. {coworker} admits it and finally explains what needs doing.
choices.journal: I asked {coworker} to explain an evasive handover note.

choices.label: Write the unfinished task into the handover
choices.title: The paper trail develops a spine
choices.result: You add the task and the next step. {coworker} likes the clarity less than they liked the alibi.
choices.journal: I documented the task missing from {coworker}’s handover.

choices.label: Confirm that you also saw absolutely nothing
choices.title: Two witnesses, no information
choices.result: {coworker} looks reassured. You now share a secret without knowing how to finish the work.
choices.journal: I joined {coworker} in avoiding a clear account of unfinished work.

after.title: The office hit list
after.body: {coworker} accidentally sends you a spreadsheet ranking everyone by who deserves to be fired. You are number one. {supervisor} has replied with a laughing face.

choices.label: Report the spreadsheet
choices.title: The joke reaches management
choices.result: {supervisor} calls it harmless until you ask to keep that explanation in writing. {coworker} deletes the sheet. Neither enjoys being documented.
choices.journal: I reported {coworker}’s firing rankings and {supervisor}’s approving reply.

choices.label: Send back your own ranking
choices.title: A competitive workplace
choices.result: Your version puts {coworker} first and {supervisor} second. They suddenly discover a policy against inappropriate spreadsheets. Your performance review acquires a new concern.
choices.journal: I retaliated against {coworker} and {supervisor} with a firing list of my own.

choices.label: Ask why you are only number one
choices.title: Room for improvement
choices.result: You demand a separate lifetime-achievement category. {coworker} laughs, then admits the spreadsheet was vicious. {supervisor} quietly removes the laughing reply.
choices.journal: I made {coworker} and {supervisor} explain my place on their firing list.

events.reason: Replace filename confusion with a coercive resignation request and an explicit genuine quit option.

before.title: FINAL_FINAL_USE_THIS_ONE
before.body: {supervisor} asks you to check a shared document. One copy is called FINAL. Another is FINAL_ACTUAL. A third is WHY_DO_I_STILL_WORK_HERE.

choices.label: Ask which one they intended to share
choices.title: Nobody mentions the third file
choices.result: {supervisor} points at the correct version with impressive speed. You return the favour by having no follow-up questions.
choices.journal: I confirmed the correct work document with {supervisor}.

choices.label: Suggest dates instead of emotional states
choices.title: A less revealing filing system
choices.result: {supervisor} agrees. The renamed copies tell you when they were written rather than how badly.
choices.journal: I suggested dated labels for confusing work documents.

choices.label: Open the most emotionally honest one
choices.title: An unrequested insight
choices.result: It is the wrong document. You learn far more about {supervisor}’s afternoon than the task required.

after.title: Your resignation, helpfully drafted
